articleTitle: Renewable Energy Conversion from Biomass
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The global impacts of fossil fuels have driven governments and companies to investigate other methods of energy production for the benefit of society. The utilization of biomass in energy validates the possibility to replace non-renewable sources of energy. Bioenergy is obtained from a wide variety of sources, including rice husks, bagasse, wood chippings, and sawdust. This article presents an examination of the techniques employed in the conversion of biomass into energy that is suitable for practical applications, ecologically friendly and also the rates at which biomass power is consumed worldwide.

articleTitle: Overview of Corrosion and its Consequences in the Oil and Gas Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This research work gave a comprehensive overview of corrosion, its mechanisms, impact, and consequences in the oil and gas industry. The corrosion phenomenon is explored, focusing on corrosion types, causes, and effects, with the aim of identifying the vast economic and environmental implications associated with it. The literature underscores the pressing need for adequate corrosion control and prevention measures to enhance efficiency, longevity, and environmental stewardship in the oil and gas industry.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an IoT based Smart Door Lock System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The Internet of thing devices are interconnected physical objects that collect and share data over the internet. IoT has the potential to revolutionize many industries, including security. Traditional door lock systems have several limitations. They are often inconvenient to use, as they require users to carry keys or enter passcodes. They are also vulnerable to physical attacks, such as lockpicking or drilling. Additionally, traditional door lock systems cannot be controlled remotely, which can be a problem if a user is away from home or needs to grant access to someone else. The proposed IoT-based smart voice and keypad door lock system using Arduino overcomes the limitations of traditional door lock systems by providing a convenient, secure, and flexible way to unlock doors. The system uses three unlocking methods: voice control, fingerprint recognition, and keypad entry. Users can choose the unlocking method that best suits their needs and preferences. Voice control enables hands-free and efficient unlocking, while fingerprint recognition offers reliable and accurate access. Keypad entry provides a balance between accuracy and ease of use. The system successfully integrates these methods, offering a robust and flexible door lock system. The proposed system has the potential to significantly improve security in a variety of settings, including homes, offices, and public spaces. It offers a convenient, secure, and accessible way to unlock doors, meeting the diverse needs of users.

articleTitle: Accounting of Carbon Footprint and Energy Consumption of Nile University in Nigeria: A detailed and Systematic Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)

articleTitle: Investigating the Performance of Doum Palm Shell as an Aggregate for Making Lightweight Interlocking Blocks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This research explored the process conducting experimental investigations on the effect of replacing coarse aggregate with doum palm shell in the properties of concrete. In Nigeria, despite having large reserves of untapped natural resources, it is important to note that resources are limited and deplete overtime, as demand for infrastructure increases. The blasting or mining of rocks for various uses has a negative impact on the environment such as: causing earth tremors, erosion, sediment runoff, fly rock, generation of dust. Hence, the need to utilize alternative materials such as: Doum palm shell, Palm kernel shell etc. that would serve as a suitable replacement in place of course aggregate which would be economical, environmentally friendly, and sustainable.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in the Application of IoT in Metallurgical Process
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This review article highlights recent advancements in applying the Internet of Things (IoT) to metallurgical processes. It focuses on the integration of Industry 4.0 technologies, adoption in emerging countries, additive manufacturing, and intelligent machining tools. IoT -enabled sensors, data analytics, and automation systems are discussed, emphasizing their real-time monitoring and control capabilities for optimizing metallurgical operations. The article also explores the challenges and successful strategies for implementing IoT in emerging countries' metallurgical industries. In additive manufacturing, IoT facilitates real-time monitoring, feedback control, and remote quality assurance. Additionally, IoT empowers intelligent machining tools with enhanced precision, reduced downtime, and increased productivity. This review contributes to the growing knowledge on leveraging IoT for improved productivity, efficiency, and quality in the metallurgical industry, promoting a sustainable and technologically advanced future.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Optimized Gas Dehydration Processes for Recovery of High Purity Glycol
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Natural gas, a valuable energy resource, requires dehydration to prevent operational issues during transportation and comply with pipeline specifications. Triethylene glycol (TEG) is commonly used for gas dehydration, and optimizing its regeneration process offers potential cost savings and operational efficiencies. This research focuses on the regeneration of triethylene glycol (TEG), which is utilized for gas dehydration in the context of natural gas processing. The aim of the research is to compare the performance of diethyl ether and cyclohexane as alternative stripping agents in TEG regeneration to the usual method, which uses methane as the stripping agent. The study's primary objectives were to identify which case achieved highest glycol purity and utilized the least energy in the reboiler. The TEG regeneration systems were simulated under optimal operating conditions using the process simulation software, Aspen HYSYS. The gathered data revealed some intriguing conclusions. The diethyl ether case had the greatest glycol concentration (99.97 wt%) and the second-lowest energy consumption in the reboiler (77,710 BTU/h). The cyclohexane case, on the other hand, had the lowest glycol concentration (98.92 wt%) and the lowest energy usage in the reboiler (74,660 BTU/h). The base case using methane as the stripping agent achieved the second-highest glycol concentration (99.62 wt%) and the highest energy consumption in the reboiler (139,400 BTU/h). These findings emphasize the importance of additional optimization and research. Future research should focus on economic analysis, conducting additional research on the cyclohexane stripping agent to maximize glycol purity, exploring alternative stripping agents, assessing environmental impact/carbon emissions, and investigating hybrid stripping approaches.

articleTitle: Enhancing Information Dissemination in Large Institutions Using Smart Screen Technology and Web Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Effective dissemination of information to audience in institutions of higher learning is a critical challenge in today's interconnected world. Conveying timely information to every individual can be arduous due to scale. Smart screens offer a dynamic solution by facilitating internet-enabled transmission of announcements to strategically positioned displays. This method ensures swift delivery of vital information to target audiences. The consequences of information gaps can be dire in urgent scenarios where missed information might be adversely affected. Both conventional and social media platforms have limitations in reaching targeted populations when distributing information. This paper aims to explore the potential of enhancing information dissemination through the fusion of smart screen technology and web applications. This strategy mitigates the risk of unintended recipients viewing urgent messages while ensuring that those intended receive it promptly. It employs a technological stack encompassing Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to provide both a robust back-end and user-friendly front-end interface. Testing, deployment, and debugging processes ensure functionality, usability, and scalability of the application. The web application test results show an overall performance of 98%. It overcame the limitations of traditional communication methods, by offering a promising avenue for future research and development, hinting at the potential for widespread implementation.

articleTitle: Green Corrosion Inhibition Practices
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Corrosion poses significant challenges for industries worldwide, causing financial losses, safety risks, and environmental issues. To address these concerns, there has been a shift towards sustainable corrosion prevention techniques. This review presents a summary of corrosion, corrosion inhibitors, and specifically focuses on green corrosion inhibitors. It discusses relevant literature exploring various types of green inhibitors to mitigate corrosion. Additionally, it highlights recent progressions in the application of green corrosion inhibitors. The insights presented in this paper enable researchers, engineers, and business experts to adopt sustainable corrosion prevention solutions.

articleTitle: Sustainable Performance of Wastewater Treatment Plant : A case study of Wupa sewage treatment plant
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This research was conducted to ascertain the sustainable performance of Wupa sewage treatment plant at Abuja Municipal Area Council, FCT. The aim of the study was to investigate the level of effectiveness of the treatment plant in removing physiochemical and bacteriological manifestations from the influent before the treated water is discharged to the Wupa River. This involved the experimental analysis of the wastewater samples collected at the influent inlet and the effluent after UV treatment by standard methods and the collation of the acquired results with NESREA and WHO standard effluent limits. The experimental analysis discovered parameters; pH, Temperature, Conductivity, Turbidity, Total Dissolved Solids, Biochemical Oxygen Demand, Total Suspended Solids, Chemical Oxygen Demand, Ammonia, Sulphate, Orthophosphate, Chloride, Dissolved oxygen, Total coliform count and Faecal coliform were observed to be 6.99, 20.6°C, 248 µf/cm, 13 NTU, 160 mg/L, 10 mg/L, 12 mg/L, 25 mg/L, 8 mg/L, 43 mg/L, 1.4 mg/L, 17 mg/L, 6.9 mg/L, 350 CFU/1mL, and 170 MPN/100mL respectively and removal efficiency of 19%, 95.5%, 92.86%, 91.66%, 93.33%, 4.44%, 36.36%, 19.05%, 95.63% and 89.38% respectively. The evaluation revealed an increase in effluent parameters of the pH, Ammonia and Total dissolved solids, although all increased values were within the specified standard discharge limits. However, even though the removal efficiency of the Turbidity was at an excellent rate of 95.5%, the effluent value 13 NTU was still above the standard effluent limit of 5 NTU. On account of the result, adequate maintenance and daily inspection of the clarifiers was encouraged, and an empirical model was created in order to improve sustainable performance of the treatment process.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Cowpea Skin, Sugar Cane Rind and Yam Bark as Additives in Water-Based Drilling Mud
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Drilling operations require the use of drilling fluid with optimum characteristics. Desired drilling fluid properties is typically controlled using additives. Due to the environmental and safety impact of synthetic additives, this research investigated the use of degradable food waste namely cowpea skin powder (CSP), sugarcane rind powder (SRP) and yam bark powder (YP) as additives in water-based drilling mud. To check the potential of these biodegradable food waste as additives, their elemental composition and approximate composition were ascertained using Scanning electron microscope with energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) and proximate analysis. The method used included the collection, cleaning, drying and grinding each of the food waste (sugarcane rind, cowpea skin and yam bark) into powdered form of 200 microns, performance evaluation of the additives was done in the concentration of 1% (5grams), 3% (10grams), 4% (15grams) and 5% (20grams) each for each API standard laboratory batch of mud. All three powders were confirmed to have significant fiber, carbon, oxygen and hydrogen content, enough to affect fluid loss and filtration control. Significant effect was observed in pH, Plastic viscosity, Yield point, Gel strength and cake thickness. The organic additives tested had no significant effect on mud density and specific gravity.

articleTitle: Distributed Generation and Its Power Quality Challenges: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This provides an overview of power quality disturbances with the integrating of distributed generation (DG) into power grids and explores potential mitigation techniques. While DG integration offers benefits such as reduced transmission losses and improved reliability and stability, it also introduces power quality challenges like voltage fluctuations, harmonics, voltage imbalance, etc. These challenges can result in equipment damage, increased downtime, and decreased consumer efficiency. To mitigate these challenges, various mitigation techniques are employed. Custom power devices (CPD) and Flexible alternate current transmission system (FACTS) devices offer effective solutions for mitigating PQ challenges. They provide control, stability, and regulation capabilities. The paper mentioned the different types of DG technology sources which are renewable and non-renewable and explores the power quality challenges and how to mitigate them using CPD, like distributed static compensator (DSTATCOM), dynamic voltage restorer (DVR), and FACTS devices like Static Var compensator (SVR), Unified power quality conditioner (UPQC) etc. Overall, it provides an understanding of power quality challenges and potential solutions to ensure cost-effective and standard power quality for end users.

articleTitle: Memory-Efficient Spike-Time-Dependent Plasticity for Future Driverless Car Park Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In addition to localization and mapping, current challenges faced by driverless (autonomous) car parks encompass computational complexity, resulting in elevated CPU utilisation and substantial memory consumption. This paper presents a memory-efficient Spike-Time-Dependent Plasticity (STDP) approach for future driverless car park infrastructure (DCPI). The proposed method utilizes self-organized mapping (SOM) classification and memory optimization techniques to analyze traffic occupancy trends. Results from geospatial data mining show optimised memory usage for vacant slots and trajectory mining clusters. Additionally, the impact of lateral suppression on STDP is demonstrated, highlighting the usefulness of STDP in managing complex memory scenarios in DCPI. Results show that STDP provides a robust neuromorphic scheme for lightweight memory utilisation particularly for tasks requiring precise timing and coordination.

articleTitle: Determination of Optimal Q and R Matrices for the LQR Control of Nonlinear BOS System Using Fish Swarm Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Q (state weighting) and R (input weighting) matrices are the essential components of the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) optimization process. Trial and error (TE) and Bryson’s methods are conventionally used for tuning them. However, these methods are time-consuming and tedious. Additionally, they do not give optimal values. Therefore, this paper uses two fish swarm algorithms, namely: artificial fish swarm algorithm (AFSA) and weighted AFSA (wAFSA), to determine the optimal Q and R matrices for the control of the ball-on-sphere (BOS) system. wAFSA was developed to solve the problem associated with AFSA of going into local minima because visual distance and step size are constant. System parameters were derived, controllability and observability were checked and optimal Q and R matrices were obtained using AFSA and wAFSA. Using these matrices, the system was controlled. Settling times of 7.0 sec, 5.70 sec, and 3.35 sec were obtained for TE, AFSA, and wAFSA, respectively. The steady-state error for the three algorithms was found to be zero. wAFSA was found to be more efficient because the objective of the control is to bring the system back to equilibrium.

articleTitle: Suitability of Agro Wastes for Biodegradable Food Packaging - A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The escalating environmental concerns surrounding the massive production and improper disposal of non-biodegradable food packaging materials have led to the urgent need for sustainable alternatives. In response to this demand, researchers have attempted the use of Agrowastes as viable alternatives. This present study aims to review some of these Agrowastes used for biodegradable food packaging. The types, compositional analysis and properties of food packages have been discussed. Applications and production processes have also been discussed. The suitability of Agrowastes as food packaging material has been highlighted. Generally, the use of Agrowastes materials as food packaging material will not only reduce impact of pollution of the environment, but will also achieve the production of food packages at reduced costs for producers.

articleTitle: Grid Integration of Wind Power System for Voltage Stability Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Integration of renewable energy for sustainable power supply is gradually securing prominence in energy deficit aversion and depletion of fossil fuels. This paper examines the impact of integration of Permanent Magnet Synchronous based Wind Turbine Generators (PMS-WTGs) on power system's voltage stability. Nigerian 52-bus, 330kV grid network is used as the study case. Successful modelling and simulation of the network were achieved in MATLAB. Ant Colony Optimization technique was used to determine optimal location and sizing of PMS-WTGs on the network. At simulation, Continuation Power Flow analysis indicates Aladja and Yola load buses as the best positions to place PMS-WTGs of respective optimal sizes of 100MW and 197MW with a 150% increase in load injection at 10% interval. The wind penetration levels maintain the ±5% bus voltage limit with the highest voltage level, 1.042p.u, at Damaturu. The overall results indicate integration of 297MW PMS-WTGs yields an improvement in voltage profile.

articleTitle: The Use of Polymer for Road Surfacing as a Strategy for Waste Recycling in Maiduguri
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The road network in Maiduguri, Borno State in Nigeria has been continuously deteriorating due to the ongoing rise in traffic combined with insufficient maintenance due to a lack of funding. Various actions, such as securing finances for maintenance, improving roadway design, using better quality materials, and using more efficient construction techniques are reported to be useful in reducing this process. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effect of polythene on the characteristics of asphalt and concrete for road surfacing as well as strategy for waste recycling. Hot bitumen and waste polymer were combined at 160°C using a strong mechanical stirrer; plastic was added to the bituminous mix using wet process techniques to create polymer-modified bitumen. Base bitumen with a penetration grade of 60/70 was used for the laboratory tests. To achieve consistency in the mixture, all the polymers were heated and chopped into pieces. 2%, 4% and 6% volume of polymer were used with a control volume of 0%. Different tests such as the Viscosity test, Flash and fire point test, Penetration test, Marshall Test, and Ductility test were all conducted using standard procedures. The test results for penetration, ductility, viscosity, flash and fire points, indicate that the material is becoming less consistent and more resistant to temperature variations. The marshal test findings showed that the modified combination had higher stability and a lower % of VMA (Voids in mineral aggregates) than the traditional plain mixtures. This would significantly increase these mixes' resistance to rutting.

articleTitle: Development of Internet of Things Circuitry for Intelligent Interactions of Smart Meters with Users
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In modern times, people’s fast-paced lifestyles make it challenging to keep track of essential recurring bills such as electricity, water, and gas. This paper proposes a unified smart metering system utilizing the Internet of Things (IoT) technology to address this need. This system comprises two interconnected sub-systems that manage resource consumption. The first subsystem is a unified metering sub-system, while the second is a cloud-controlled sub-system that stores and analyzes data. Both sub-systems communicate wirelessly, and the server is automatically updated as resources are consumed. The design employs an intelligent interaction approach that leverages information and communication technologies to improve user experiences, task performance, and quality of life. The expected outcome is the development of a mobile application that integrates a billing portal for payment processing. The implementation of this solution is expected to enhance resource utilization, promote sustainability practices, and revolutionize the user experience of interacting with utility services.

articleTitle: Development of hydrometallurgical purification process for Nigerian gypsum ore in hydrochloric acid. Part II: Recovery of pure gypsum from leached liquor
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: As the world grapples with the challenges of resource scarcity and sustainability, the need to develop indigenous raw materials has gained paramount importance. To achieve self-sufficiency and reduce dependence on foreign sources, harnessing hydrometallurgical processes to extract valuable elements from ores presents a promising solution. Raw gypsum from Postikum, Nigeria, was leached in hydrochloric acid to obtain a pure calcium sulphate dihydrate. The dissolution kinetics have been reported elsewhere. This present study focused on optimizing the recovery of pure gypsum by varying acid concentration, temperature, and solid-liquid ratio. Additionally, the recyclability of regenerated hydrochloric acid was tested. The characterization of the raw gypsum ore (RWG), leached residue (LR), and recovered pure gypsum (RCG) was done using SEM-EDS, XRF, and XRD, respectively. The recovered gypsum was characterised by a brilliant white colour in contrast to the initial brown colour of the ore. XRF results show that RWG contains 50.48% SO3 while RCG contains 57.72 %. XRD results revealed that RWG contains gypsum, magnesite, mordenite, witherite, and calcite, LR contains mordenite, witherite and quartz while RCG consists of gypsum crystal phase only with no impurities. Remarkably, 85% RCG was successfully recovered at the fourth recycle stage of HCl lixiviant. These findings demonstrate that hydrometallurgical treatment of gypsum ore with hydrochloric acid can produce very pure gypsum.

articleTitle: Optimized SVM - Based Network Anomaly Detection with Genetic Algorithm and Recursive Feature Elimination
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Network anomaly detection is a critical task in cybersecurity which aims to identify unusual patterns and potential threats in network traffic. Existing solutions often rely on machine learning (ML) algorithms, including support vector machines (SVMs). However, traditional SVMs with fixed kernels may struggle to capture complex, non-linear relationships in network data, leading to suboptimal detection performance. Additionally, selecting the right hyperparameters is often a non-trivial task. In this paper, we investigate the application of SVMs with varying kernels (linear, sigmoid, polynomial, and radial basis function (RBF)) for network anomaly detection. We extend our exploration to RBF kernel optimization using genetic algorithm (GA) to fine-tune critical hyperparameters (C and Gamma). Concurrently, we integrate recursive feature elimination (RFE) for optimal feature selection, enhancing the model's discriminatory prowess. To evaluate our proposed method, our study encompasses a standard dataset of over 40,000 training instances and 40+ features, subjected to meticulous preprocessing. Rigorous evaluation using 10-fold cross-validation was performed culminating in a final validation on a distinct test dataset. Our empirical results show the supremacy of the GA-RBF-SVM model, driven by GA-optimized hyperparameters, in conjunction with RFE compared to the other SVM variants. This configuration achieves exceptional performance with 99.39% accuracy on validation data and 99.46% on the test dataset. Additionally, our study extends to advanced (ensemble) ML techniques all demonstrating exceptional performance benchmarks. This study demonstrates that with systematic parameter optimization and appropriate feature selection, RBF-kernel based SVMs can perform competitively in network anomaly detection compared to advanced machine learning schemes.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Optimization in Massive MIMO Systems with Low-Resolution ADCs
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) is a promising 5G technology, but the high energy consumption from numerous radio components is a key challenge. Prior work has explored higher than 4-bit ADCs, but very low 1-2 bit remain uninvestigated. This paper provides an in-depth examination of the resolution versus power savings and signal quality degradation trade-offs with 1–3-bit analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) in Massive MIMO systems. Mathematical modeling and simulations quantify the exponential reduction in power consumption along with losses in key performance metrics like signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), throughput, and spectral efficiency with lower ADC resolutions stemming from increased quantization noise. Advanced linear detection techniques are shown to effectively recover the signal quality degradation. The analysis provides valuable insights on jointly optimizing ADC configuration and signal processing to maximize overall system efficiency. Energy savings of over 50% are demonstrated with 1-bit ADCs along with the ability to maintain acceptable performance metrics using linear detectors. The practical implementation feasibility is also discussed. This work enables ultra-low-resolution ADC deployments in energy-efficient Massive MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an Enhanced Dynamic Knowledge-Based Authentication System (EDKBA) in the Era of Social Media
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Services related to information and communication technology (ICT) today require secure personal identity verification methods to guard against unauthorized access. There are several authentication methods, with traditional passwords being the most popular one. Passwords are susceptible to threats like eavesdropping and forgotten passwords, though. One of the finest substitutes for conventional passwords was knowledge-based authentication (KBA), which verifies identification using public records. Static and dynamic KBAs are examples of KBAs that are vulnerable to theft and modification. The goal of the study was to develop and implement an enhanced DKBA (EDKBA) system that uses challenge response questions and answers to authenticate users in real time. Two attack models, naive attack (guessing) and strategic attack (brute force), were used to evaluate the effectiveness of the EDKBA system. The developed EDKBA provided improved security by dynamically generating authentication questions based on real-time information about users' weekly Facebook activities. The EDKBA experiment showed a success rate and True Positive of 72.57% with an acceptable error rate (False Negative) of 27.43%. The study concluded that implementing EDKBA will reduce the rising risks brought on by unauthorized access to data and cybercrime, which would directly improve the overall security of sensitive data and information.

articleTitle: Effect of Sawdust and Coconut Fiber Particles on the viscosity of Water-Based Mud
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The viscosifying additives used in drilling operations commonly include imported organic polymers like carboxymethyl cellulose and polyanionic cellulose (PAC). The over-reliance on these imported additives in some countries consumes their scarce foreign exchange and increases the Capital expenditure (CAPEX) of the drilling operation. Consequently, cheap, and easily accessible local materials that can perform a similar role are being considered as potential substitutes. This research was conducted to examine the effect of sawdust, coconut fiber and a composite of sawdust and the coconut fiber as a potential viscosifying additive in water-based drilling mud, and the outcomes were compared with carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC). Furthermore, in order to ascertain the best combination ratio for the sawdust and coconut fiber to achieved optimal viscosifying result. The study experimented on three combinations (50:50,75:25, and 25:75) in a 5g concentration of 350ml water-based mud. Ofite Rotational Viscometer was used for measurement of the viscosity. The result shows that sawdust particles are better viscosifying agents when compared to coconut fiber particles and any composite mix of sawdust and coconut fiber particles. In addition, the results show that coconut fiber particles behave as a mud thinning agent as it reduces the viscosity of the water-based drilling mud. The empirical data further indicates that a sawdust mud concentration of 2.5g gave a higher plastic viscosity of 11.3 centipoise when compared to a 2.5g mud concentration of CMC which gave a plastic viscosity value of 9.8 centipoise. The research study also presented values of yield point and gel strength for the nine formulated samples of sawdust, coconut fiber, sawdust and coconut fiber composite and CMC.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of the REBA and RULA Assessment Tools Efficiency for Workers Tasks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This article compares the usefulness of two well- known ergonomic assessment procedures, the Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) and the Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA), in determining the ergonomic hazards associated with employees' duties. With the rising emphasis on occupational health and well-being, the selection of suitable evaluation instruments plays a vital role in avoiding musculoskeletal diseases (MSDs) and promoting workers productivity. conducting this comparative review and analysis, a comprehensive method involving the examination of past works that focused on REBA and RULA assessments was employed. These works were selected based on their relevance and rigor in evaluating the ergonomic hazards associated with different job tasks. The study critically explores the methodology, strengths, limits, and practical applications of REBA and RULA within distinct work settings. By diving into the deep variations between these techniques, the study gives significant insights for practitioners, academics, and policymakers trying to enhance ergonomic evaluations and promote a healthier and safer workplace. This paper finds that the REBA evaluation tool is adaptable across industries but requires training for accurate use, while the RULA assessment tool is simpler but may not suit complex tasks. The choice between them should consider workplace needs and limitations, like job duration and hand-arm vibration risk. A nuanced approach, combining both tools and expert opinion, is recommended for accurate ergonomic evaluations.

articleTitle: Sensor Technology for Car Park Management System: Nile University of Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The escalating parking space problem at Nile University of Nigeria poses a growing threat due to rising enrollments. The absence of a structured parking management system compounds this issue. This project aims to develop a system to inform users about available parking slots, mitigating parking congestion, and providing valuable insights for carpark management improvements

articleTitle: Application and Emerging Properties of HSS X65 Pipe in the Oil and Gas Industry-Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The study provides an in-depth exploration of the High-Strength Steel (HSS) X65 pipe, a material that's become pivotal in the oil and gas industry due to its exceptional strength, toughness, and corrosion resistance. The review delves into its principal applications within the sector, including its role in long-distance pipelines, risers, flow lines, and as structural components. The unique mechanical properties of the HSS X65 pipe, such as its ability to withstand high pressure, resist corrosive influences, and maintain structural integrity in varying environments, are outlined. Furthermore, the paper investigates the recent advancements enhancing the X65 pipe's performance and service life, such as microstructure refinement techniques, corrosion resistance improvements, and the innovative application of digital twin technology. These developments not only augment the material's existing properties but also open avenues for more cost-effective and resilient solutions in the oil and gas industry.

articleTitle: Assessment of Tricycle Operation as a Transportation System in Minna, Niger State
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In this study conducted in Minna, Nigeria, the focus was on the use of tricycles as a transportation system. The main objectives were to assess the level of driving knowledge among tricycle operators, identify the challenges they encounter, and propose potential solutions to address these issues. To gather data, a mixed-methods approach combining surveys and interviews was employed with tricycle operators. A questionnaire was used to evaluate the operators' driving knowledge, covering topics such as road safety, traffic regulations, and specific operational procedures related to tricycle operation. The collected data provided valuable insights into areas where operators lacked knowledge and areas that needed improvement. Additionally, the study investigated the challenges faced by tricycle operators in Minna, including traffic congestion, inadequate infrastructure, safety concerns, difficulties in obtaining permits and licenses, absence of parking or waiting areas, and high operating costs. Through interviews with the operators and stakeholders, the study aimed to understand the extent and impact of these challenges on their daily operations. Based on the findings, several solutions were proposed to address the identified challenges. These solutions encompassed implementing traffic management strategies to alleviate congestion, improving infrastructure to accommodate tricycles, enhancing safety measures through training and enforcement, streamlining the permit and licensing process, providing designated parking areas, and exploring options for reducing costs and offering financial support to tricycle operators. The study's findings and proposed solutions contribute to a better understanding of tricycle operation in Minna and provide valuable insights for policymakers, transportation authorities, and stakeholders to enhance the efficiency, safety, and sustainability of tricycle transportation in the city. It is recommended to further research and collaborate among relevant parties to implement and evaluate the effectiveness of these proposed solutions.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization Algorithm for Reducing Energy Consumption in a Smart Home
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The importance of electricity to humanity cannot be overstated. The dependence of human beings on this very precious resource has caused a strain on its production as the growing demand is far outweighing the speed at which the supply can be ramped up. Furthermore, this explosion of demand has caused an even more significant problem of price gouging leading to costly utility bills and energy insecurity for the residential consumers. However, in recent years, the enormous leaps made in smart grid technology and internet of things (IoT) have brought a renewed enthusiasm in the research space as these two technologies when combined, have brought about breakthroughs in smart home automation. The primary focus of this study is to develop a smart home automation algorithm that can be used to reduce electricity consumption at home. The algorithm combines two essential electricity optimization methods which are appliance scheduling and environmental condition to provide an optimal energy consumption pattern. Sensor data from PIR, ambient light and temperature sensors are fed real-time into the algorithm to make appropriate decisions regarding appliance status. When this algorithm was simulated on a modeled home using a virtual human behaviour table, 68% energy saving of the maximum energy consumption of the house was achieved. This shows that the algorithm can provide a substantial energy savings which vary from consumer to consumer depending on their movement while in the house, specified environmental conditions and preset appliance schedule.

articleTitle: Implementing Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Enhanced Trajectory Tracking and Road Anomaly Avoidance in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving realm of autonomous vehicles, trajectory tracking stands as a cornerstone for ensuring safety and precision in navigation. Traditional linear methodologies, although efficient to some extent, can be inadequate in addressing the challenges posed by complex urban environments and defective roads. Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC), with its capability to anticipate future events and adapt accordingly, presents an opportunity to redefine the trajectory tracking landscape. Therefore, this study presents the integration of NMPC for trajectory tracking in autonomous vehicles. Through a comprehensive analysis and simulations, this study showcases improved tracking accuracy, and enhanced adaptability in diverse scenarios. Our findings underscore the potential of NMPC in setting a new benchmark for trajectory tracking, ultimately pushing the boundaries of what autonomous vehicles can achieve.

articleTitle: Iot Based Home Automation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is fast expanding and is projected to pervade practically every area of daily life. The concept of Internet of Things (IoT) requires the seamless connectivity of millions of heterogeneous devices. Smart homes, smart cities, health care, smart agriculture, logistics and retail, and even smart ecosystems are all viable sectors for IoT use. However, a modern smart city or smart home that offers a variety of and complicated functions with hybrid communication networks has not been able to meet the needs of basic IoT systems. In order to handle and analyze big data and deal with the issues of finding the best solution, making the best decision, recognizing events, and identifying objects, modern applications of IoT systems require the assistance of sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) technology. Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to any system that can understand its surroundings and take measures to increase its chances of success. Thinking rationally, acting defensibly, and acting like a human being are the ideal state of artificial intelligence. This article highlights the most cutting-edge ways that Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques is being used in homes to make them smarter, more automated, and more digital in many ways. The literature described a variety of IoT and AI applications, systems, and approaches and reported their findings.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Semantic Segmentation Models for Identification of Sweet Potato Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Semantic segmentation models have been proposed to identify plant leaf diseases. However, these models need to be evaluated on different datasets and applications for validation of model performance and deployment on edge devices. This research carried out performance evaluation of U-Net, Compressed U-Net, SegNet and PSPNet segmentation models to identify early and late blight diseased leaf images of Sweet potato. The image dataset was obtained from Plant village dataset. Three hundred leaf images were manually annotated using VGG Image Annotator (VIA) tool. Python programming language version 3.10.6 was used to implement the models. The dataset was split into 70% for training, 20% for validation and 10% for testing. The results of evaluation of the models showed that the Compressed U-Net outperformed other models for the dataset. The compressed U-Net requires only 7.9% of space needed by standard U-Net model and inference time for predicting the potato diseased leaves is good without compromise with mean intersection over union. This work recommends evaluating the performance of Compressed U-Net on diseased leaves of different crops and deploying the model on edge devices such as Raspberry Pi, smartphones to validate the model results.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of Broadband Quadrature Modulator Using 90° Coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This paper presents a wide-band quadrature modulator's design, simulation, and performance evaluation using a 90°-hybrid coupler. Three different center frequencies of 3.0 GHz, 3.5 GHz, and 4.0 GHz were studied. The hybrid couplers are used in communication devices such as power combiners, amplifiers, mixers, dividers, and modulators. The four-port component splits the output signal with a resulting 90° phase shift while maintaining excellent output port isolation. The coupler was first designed and synthesized using ADS design tools, and the branch lengths (L) and widths (W) of the sections were then optimized in the schematic structure to get the ideal needed values. Then, excitation and simulation were performed using the Keysight ADS Momentum tool at the 2.5D EM simulator. The performance of the device at three different center frequencies was evaluated in terms of bandwidth, insertion loss, and phased difference, and found that the device operating at 3.5GHz center frequency was the best and in good correlation with the ideal quadrature modulator available in the literature.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle: Prospects and Possibility in Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The rate at which the global automotive industry advances in technology with its attendant benefits in eco-friendliness has become a wake-up thought to Nigerian automotive industries. With the available resources and technical know-how in Nigeria for the production of internal combustion engine (ICE) automobile, there should be nascent interest and political will to produce Electric Vehicles (EVs) as well in Nigeria. However, the challenges of insufficient, unstable electricity supply, good road network, procurement of batteries and provision of charging facilities critical for the EVs will have to be tackled to realise the vision as elucidated in this study. It is hoped that the recommendations prescribed would be a good roadmap for a promising country like Nigeria to compete favourably with other developed countries in EV production.

articleTitle: Review of Construction Methods used in Ongoing Projects in Nile University Campus: Adapting Proposed Modern Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This project offers a comprehensive assessment of the construction methods implemented in the ongoing projects taking place at Nile University Campus, with a particular emphasis on the integration of proposed modern technologies. The aim is to analyze the construction techniques and technologies employed in these projects and evaluate their effectiveness in terms of time, cost, quality, and sustainability. The review commences by providing an overview of Nile University Campus and its ongoing construction projects. It subsequently explores the examination of conventional construction methods commonly utilized in the region, highlighting their limitations and challenges. The subsequent section concentrates on the suggested modern technology solutions that have the potential to enhance the construction process. Various contemporary construction techniques, including Building Information Modeling (BIM), prefabrication, modular construction, and sustainable building practices, among others, are evaluated in this paper. Their potential benefits, such as improved project efficiency, reduced construction time, enhanced quality control, and minimized environmental impact, are thoroughly examined.

articleTitle: A Review on Biomass Conversion Process for Bioenergy Production
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The expansion of the global population has increased the demand for renewable and environmentally friendly energy. This resulted in the search for alternative energy sources, especially those that utilise industrial refuse, such as biomass. Biomass can be converted into biofuels and bioenergy that meet the requirements of society while also having a lower environmental impact, and the materials are frequently inexpensive and easily accessible. Utilising biomass as a source of energy has the added benefit of generating employment opportunities in underdeveloped and undeveloped regions worldwide. This review examines the current energy situation and methods for transforming biomass into energy, underscoring the significance of understanding the properties of biomass materials in order to reduce dependence on fossil fuels.

articleTitle: Density functional theory study of adsorption pathways of TiCl4 on Polyether Ether Ketone
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In this study, a theoretical evaluation was conducted on the adsorption pathway of TiCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> on PEEK at room temperature (298 K) and pressure (101325 Pa). The thermodynamics of the complexation process on the ketone and ether functional groups were described using density functional theory. It was found that the adsorption of TiCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> at room temperature was not spontaneous, but it could be achieved by reducing the reacting temperature. The adsorption process only occurred through coordination to form a pentacoordinate TiCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>-PEEK complex without dissociation. Moreover, dissociative chemisorption was not preferred. TiCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> only interacted with the carbonyl group when the carbonyl group was normal to the surface or slightly inclined, and not when it was parallel to the surface. There was no interaction between the TiCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and the ether group.

articleTitle: Utilization of Bacillus subtilis and Aspergillus niger for the Bioremediation of Heavy Metals in the WUPA Wastewater Treatment Plant, Abuja
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Safe discharge of untreated wastewater and scarcity of water is still a burning problem in front of mankind. The study was undertaken to assess the potentials of Bacillus subtilis and Aspergillus niger for remediation potentials in wastewater. The wastewater samples (influent and effluent) were analyzed for physiochemical parameters and heavy metals analysis and compared against WHO specification for water quality. All physiochemical parameters for both effluent and influent (pH, Temperature, Conductivity, Turbidity, TDS, TSS, BOD, COD, Nitrate, and Sulphate) were within specifications except for high turbidity of 181 NTU recorded for influent wastewater against WHO specification of (<40 NTU). and heavy metal analysis was carried out before and after treatment of the wastewater. The result shows the heavy metals analyzed for each wastewater were within World Health Organization (WHO) specifications with the exceptions of Mn: 0.31 mg/l and Fe: 0.91 mg/l present in the influent wastewater which were above WHO specifications (Mn: 0.05 mg/l and Fe: 0.30 mg/l). Bioaugmentation activities were analyzed for both Bacillus subtilis and Aspergillus niger for both influent and effluent wastewater. The removal of heavy metal was determined using AAS and results reveals that the introduction of Bacillus subtilis and Aspergillus niger in the influent wastewater did not remediate the heavy metals as expected but for the effluent wastewater the bioaugmentation activity of Bacillus subtilis and Aspergillus niger individually show good remediation potentials as it reduce the heavy metals (Mn, Fe, and Zn) within WHO specification against their initial concentrations. In conclusion Bacillus subtilis has more remediation potential than Aspergillus niger when bioaugmented in wastewater.

articleTitle: Probing Mechanical Properties: Tools for Investigating Solid Polymer Electrolytes
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have become an essential energy storage technology for a variety of applications, such as energy storage systems, electric vehicles, and flexible electronics. However, due to safety concerns regarding the flammability of the liquid electrolytes used in conventional LIBs, their use has been restricted; thus, there is considerable interest in the use of solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) and other solid electrolytes. These SPEs inhibit the growth of lithium dendrites and prevent thermal runaway, which is responsible for the instability of liquid electrolytes. Despite this, SPEs have inferior mechanical properties, resulting in a reduced battery cycle life. Thus, SPEs have been modified by incorporating particles, particularly nanoparticles, into their polymer matrix in order to improve their mechanical properties. Due to their inherent properties, including a large surface area and mechanical rigidity, these nanoparticles improve the interfacial contact and electrochemical stability of these modified SPEs. Consequently, it is essential to investigate the mechanical properties of these SPEs using appropriate techniques. Even though numerous reports have investigated the mechanical properties of some of these SPEs, there is insufficient literature on the tools/techniques for analyzing these mechanical properties. In this review, the experimental techniques used to explore the mechanical properties of SPEs are described.

articleTitle: Mutation Testing Techniques for Android Applications: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Mobile applications are becoming increasingly used to achieve various computing needs. Hence, it is essential to guarantee quality of the applications. Software testing has been the main activity for ensuring the quality of software, however, it is a critical and costly activity. Furthermore, code coverage is commonly used as metric for verifying the effectiveness of testing technique. However, numerous researchers and experts claimed that considering code coverage only to ascertain the testing quality is not enough to ensure quality of apps. In view of this, mutation testing has been introduced to complement the procedure by assuring that apps behave as expected and are released free of faults. Several techniques/tools were proposed based on different syntax and mutation operators. This study presents a comparative study of six (6) mutation techniques/tools for Android applications to highlight their strengths and weakness which will give an insight to researchers on the directions for further research.

articleTitle: ASTM Method for Inclusion Analysis of Prepared Green Steel
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In the present situation, steel-making industries have turned their attention towards producing quality steel, through more feasible routes. One of the routes is the production of green steel, which is a kind of steel produced through a process which reduces the emission of carbon dioxide. Steel produced through traditional methods relies heavily on fossil fuel and coal, emitting large amounts of CO2, resulting in 6 – 7 % of global greenhouse gas emissions. Eventually, steel production using blast furnaces requires coking coal, which has limited reserves in India. An alternative approach to this is the utilization of DRI which consumes either non-coking coal or Hydrogen for its reduction, which significantly reduces carbon emission. To produce clean steel, it is necessary to undergo a complete assessment of the Non-Metallic Inclusions (NMI). Often, Types, sizes and distribution of Non-Metallic Inclusions play a major role in the steel properties. The present study has been performed to investigate the inclusion rating of steel produced from hydrogen-based DRI (HDRI) during steel making in an Induction Furnace (IF) and carbon-based DRI to understand the cleanness of steel as per ASTM E-45 standard. The kinetics of inclusion formation during steel making in induction furnaces has been studied using Classical Nucleation Theory. Thermodynamic modelling of different types of inclusion formation was carried out using the Fact Sage software package and it has been validated experimentally with the inclusion classifier of the SEM/EDS analyzer.

articleTitle: Space Requirement-Anthropometric Parameter-Whole Body Vibration Discrepancies during Earthmoving Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Several reports have linked musculoskeletal and lower spine disorders to long term exposure to whole body vibration (WBV), maintaining awkward postures, lifting maximum loads among others. Most times, exact cause(s) of these disorders aren’t clear. This study, in attempt to investigating causes of musculoskeletal and lower spine disorders, the space where operators of earthmoving equipment are occupying vis-à-vis their anthropometric parameters were compared. A datasheet to collect anthropometric parameter of the operators and the working space requirement was designed and data were collected using anthropometers (in this case rules and standiometer) in certain construction sites in Ekiti and Ondo States, Nigeria.

articleTitle: The Preparation Techniques and Application of Aluminium Metal Matrix Composites: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Aluminium Metal Matrix Composites (AMMCs) have developed into a class of sophisticated materials with the potential to transform several engineering manufacturing sectors, by combining the lightweight features of aluminium with materials of better mechanical, thermal, and wear properties. This paper presents a complete examination of AMMCs, spanning their fundamental ideas, matrix-reinforcement combinations, processing techniques, mechanical characteristics and engineering applications. The integration of varied reinforcing phases, such as ceramic particles and fibres, inside an aluminium matrix is explored, highlighting the ensuing benefits in strength, stiffness, wear resistance, and thermal stability. Various processing methods, from powder metallurgy to liquid-phase processes, are examined in the context of their influence on composite features. The research explores the mechanical characteristics of AMMCs, offering light on their potential for aerospace, automotive, electronics, and consumer product applications. This review presents a thorough perspective on the current status of Aluminium Metal Matrix Composites, providing significant information resources for academics, engineers, and enterprises researching the dynamic terrain of new materials.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Foreign Object Impact on Polymer-Based Composites Used in Aircraft Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of foreign object damage on the damage morphology of polymer-based composite structures used in aircraft manufacture. Specimen made from E-glass laminates with epoxy matrix was subjected to quasi-static loading while acoustic emission, as well as scanning electron microscopy, were used to characterize the damage sequence. The study finds that the load-bearing capacity of the specimen impacted by the square indenter is five times more than that for the conical indenter (2.4 KN and 0.48 KN) respectively while the samples subjected to conical indenter absorbed only 13% of the energy of the samples subjected to the blunt indenter before fracture (7.9 J and 1.3 J) respectively. Furthermore, the use of acoustic emission provided a veritable measure for assessing the internal damage mechanism for structural optimization. The major failure modes identified are fibre breakage, matric crack, and delamination.

articleTitle: Production of Bioplastics Using Yam and Plantain Peels and their Biodegradability Potentials
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This study endeavors to fabricate bioplastic specimens utilizing plantain and yam peels, incorporating diverse proportions of plasticizers. Glycerol and sorbitol were employed individually as plasticizers to enhance the malleability of the material. A comprehensive analysis of the distinct physical and chemical attributes (including moisture content, water absorption, soil biodegradation, and tensile strength) resulting from diverse compositions was conducted by generating five samples for each type of bioplastic. These specimens were formulated utilizing varied quantities and combinations of plasticizers. The distinctive characteristics of the bioplastic samples render them highly adaptable for a broad spectrum of applications. All ten specimens were engineered utilizing natural and ecologically benign raw materials, manifesting biodegradability and thereby affirming their potential as an environmentally sustainable substitute for traditional plastics.

articleTitle: Overview of Ancillary Services in the Nigerian Power Sector
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: An overview of the ancillary services in the Nigerian power sector is provided in this work. These services are essential in the power system because they are additional services required by the grid during critical times to enable the power grid to operate in a stable, safe, and reliable manner. The ancillary services provided as stipulated in the Grid Code are black start, frequency control, operating reserves, and voltage control. The System Operator procures the relevant ancillary service depending on the requirement of the grid at a particular time. The paper further presents some ways of improving the viability of ancillary services for the energy grid of Nigeria. These include making incentives more attractive for suppliers of ancillary services, utilizing more hydroelectric power plants for generation and load balancing, integrating distributed generation to provide support to the reactive power, and making necessary investments in the grid.

articleTitle: Physico-chemical Characterization of Date Palm Seed as A Reinforcement in Aluminium Matrix Composites
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This study investigates the use of date palm seed as a potential reinforcement material in aluminum composites. Two samples of date palm seed (non-ash and ash) were prepared through crushing and calcination in an electric muffle furnace at 500°C. FTIR tests and X-ray fluorescence analysis were conducted on the samples. The results showed that the raw date palm seed sample contained functional groups like hydroxyl/phenol, alkane, and alkene, while the date palm seed ash contained only alkene. The XRF analysis revealed similar oxides found in other agro-wastes used as reinforcement materials. The main oxide in the date seed ash was potassium oxide, while the main oxide in the raw date palm seed was magnesium oxide. Elemental analysis revealed the presence of iron, potassium, chromium, and magnesium in both date palm seed samples.

articleTitle: Queuing System in E-commerce: An approach to Strengthen its Security
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The absence of client security and privacy online is explored, and a few strategies to bring about change are suggested. Security and privacy are issues that have been having detrimental or negative consequences on the ongoing development and growth of E-commerce. Hence, the need for a system with a secured administrator interface that can identify customers, view and show list of customers, and able to disable and enable customers through usernames and password verification with a well-designed portal with an encryption cryptographic algorithm for secured business transactions is desired. The design of an E-commerce cloud application model called Cloud E-commerce System (CES) is developed using an analytical model for server resource management using Poisson and exponential traffic distribution. The results showed that the Ecommerce server network model demonstrated a similarity response in the 92% throughput metric with a significant disparity in the 22% utilization response that can favour a clouded throughput and service utilizations which are important metrics for enterprise web application deployments.

articleTitle: Schematic Design of a Water Supply Treatment Purification Plant for Nile University of Nigeria Campus
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The present study investigated the water quality across the seven locations chosen within the study area, of which nine parameters were tested on each collected sample using various equipment’s and observed to show varying values across the different locations. The various locations of which the samples were chosen were selected as they serve as direct access points for water to the consumers. After analysis of the parameters using the weighted arithmetic index method and evaluation of results obtained from the water quality analysis of the water consumed within the study area, the Water Quality Index (WQI) was determined, and it can be seen by the values of the WQI calculated for each sample having values which range from 52.40-61.84 which fall under 51-75 range of the water quality index rating which indicates poor water quality. This indicates a need for a water treatment purification plant to ensure water of adequate quality and quantity is provided across all locations where it might be required. The location of the proposed treatment plant was also chosen based on its proximity to the intake source of water and the various components of the treatment plant were designed to eliminate and remove both suspended and dissolved impurities.

articleTitle: Using Mechatronics to Facilitate Manufacturing Processes
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Carrying out large-scale industrial processes has always been a problem for manufacturers. Most especially processes that require a lot of precision over a lot of units being manufactured or assembled. Traditionally, human beings have been used to carry out such processes. For example, on car assembly lines. The downside about using human labour for this is that it is time and capital intensive. The work is done slowly. Also, human labour entails a lot of variables which lead to unnecessary inefficiencies. Mechatronics systems, which include robotic arms, grippers and conveyor belts, have been created to handle these complex processes. These systems have the ability to carry out these complex processes due to the sensors and advanced control algorithms they are equipped with. This enables them to perform precise and repeatable movements, hence ensuring quality and consistency in the manufactured product. Mechatronics has contributed to the resolution of the problem of industrial automation by offering cutting-edge solutions for handling and placing complicated parts, integrating various manufacturing processes, and enhancing the precision and efficiency of production operations. Manufacturing businesses may now increase their competitiveness and meet the rising demand for high-quality products thanks to these solutions.

articleTitle: Strategies, Problems and Prospects of Refuse Management in Nile University of Nigeria Campus
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Nile University is an environment for learning, so the school must adhere to the standards of the state to keep the environment conducive because it’s crucial for the health and well-being of the people living in the community. Despite the population, public enlightenment on environmental health should be carried out because improper refuse management can have serious consequences for public health and the environment. Unauthorized disposal of waste in areas not designated for waste disposal can influence the public’s health and the environment of Nile University. This study provides a systematic review of efforts to overcome these challenges in the context of inappropriate recycling protocols of waste and their toxic effects on human health and the environment. The questionnaire survey included several inquiries on recycling programs, awareness campaigns, and general satisfaction with the garbage management system. To ensure diversity across the university, a sample of students and employees from various departments was chosen.

articleTitle: An Efficient Narrowband Null-Steering Beamformer for Interference Mitigation in Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In wireless communication systems, it is frequently preferable to use a null steering beamformer to reduce interference from strong narrowband signals and other multi-path signals. This paper proposes an efficient narrowband null-steering beamformer based on an Improved Davies Narrowband Null-steering (IDNN) algorithm combined with an Improved Constant Modulus Algorithm (ICMA). The designed beamformer can impose adaptive nulls at interferences without knowing directions in the side lobe region by employing the ICMA for signal adaptation, while maintaining the main lobe toward the desired user direction. The results reveal that the developed beamformer increased the convergence rate by 12.8%, as seen by lower output power convergence when compared to the traditional Davies Narrowband Null-steering (DNN) algorithm. Thus, the new algorithm is observed to have much faster convergence behavior.

articleTitle: Investigating the Most Influential Factors for Customer Satisfaction in Online Stores
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: It is important to business owners and managers to understand their customers changing needs. Understanding the most important factors that influence their customers about their products and services is key to achieving this objective. This work presents a systematic method for determining the factors that have the greatest influence on customer satisfaction in an online stores. This is crucial for determining the degree of customer satisfaction. In order to achieve this, we relied on existing literature of customer satisfaction, respondents’ responses to academic questionnaires and statistical correlations. The output from this work is a ranking of the most influential factors for customers’ satisfaction. This is important to business owners and managers in order to better understand the aspects of their business to closely monitor so as to achieve higher customer satisfaction which in turn leads to re-purchase decisions.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Path Loss Models for Wireless Communications at 3.5 GHz and 23 GHz in a Regular Urban Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Accurate channel models are required to evaluate the performance of mobile communication systems and optimize coverage for existing and future wireless networks. To improve two of the most widely used empirical path loss models; 3GPP and CI, this paper considered the elevation angle from the receiver to the transmitter to evaluate 5G coverage in real scenarios of a regular urban environment at 3.5 GHz. Measurement campaigns were carried out to evaluate the chosen models' accuracy in the 3.5 GHz environment, while simulation experiments for the environment under consideration at the 23 GHz channel were carried out using an RF planning software tool, Path Loss 5 (PL5). The assessment criteria of Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) were used to test the outcomes of the changes to the path loss prediction models. With a path loss exponent of 3.1, the model comparison showed that, at a 3.5 GHz channel, the enhanced 3GPP and CI models outperformed the conventional models in both scenarios. The 3GPP outperformed admirably on the 23 GHz channel with an MAE of 5.41 dB and 7.32 dB in both scenarios (LoS and NLoS), while the CI model underestimates the path loss. This indicates that the improved models are highly suitable for use in an outdoor regular urban environment.

articleTitle: A Framework for Internet Protocol Based Realtime Bottle Inspection System Using Blobanalysis Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Image processing is becoming a more significant component of the production process in order to define the efficiency and accuracy of the bottles. This paper presents an automatic vision inspection system that employs a stream of real-time videos recorded from the Android camera and sent to MATLAB through wireless network to improve line quality, In the vision inspection, methods and algorithms were employed to analyze and detect the presence and attributes of a bottle, then extract useful data using a Graphical User Interface. Filtering, segmentation, and blob analysis were used to remove most noise and undesired objects. The system's testing findings demonstrate that it is accurate when the camera is placed in a steady, fixed distance from the bottle and at a fixed motor speed. However, results may be impacted by a high motor speed. Anomaly detection has also advanced to a high level with strong detection accuracy.

articleTitle: A Review on Smart Traffic Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This System holds significant potential to elevate traffic management efforts and bolster road safety within urban environments. The Smart Connected Traffic Management System is a web-based application developed using the Dash framework. The system offers real-time control and monitoring capabilities for traffic lights, along with a comprehensive suite of traffic statistics, aimed at improving the efficiency of traffic management. This implementation harnesses libraries like Dash, Dash Bootstrap Components, and Dash DAQ to construct a responsive and visually appealing user interface. Notably, the traffic control module enables seamless toggling between “Normal” and “Emergency” traffic modes. With its modular code structure and user-friendly design, the system remains poised for future expansion, including the integration of IoT devices.

articleTitle: Broadband Rectifiers for Radio Frequency Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Our environment is blessed with abundant Radio Frequency (RF) energy which can be harvested to provide a steady power supply to low-powered devices such as wireless sensors, Internet of Thing devices etc. Broadband rectifiers are devices that can harvest RF energy over a wide range of frequencies. They have the advantage of collecting RF energy as much as possible over wide frequency spectrum. However, designing a broadband rectifier is very challenging. This paper presents a review of broadband rectifiers for RF energy harvesting. A good rectifier must be compact, efficient and simple in design. From the works reviewed, it was observed that the most commonly used topology for designing a broadband rectifier are the voltage doubler and the shunt rectifier topology. The most compact rectifier has a size of 37×10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Convergence of Blockchain, AI and IoT for Effective Monitoring and Securing Smart City Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The convergence of block chain, artificial intelligence, and the internet of things (IoT) for effective monitoring and securing smart city infrastructure combines these three hot trends in technology and promises to advance the development of smart cities. Blockchain, AI, and IoT represent one of the most notable technological revolutions since the combination of computing and transaction processing systems, which is now having a positive impact. Due to the actions of cyber assault, the applications of these technologies will soon have such a significant impact on our society that it will be difficult to picture life without them. The Internet of Things Infrastructure is vulnerable to assaults since it is hosted on the cloud. Modern methods are thoroughly examined to talk about the advantages and difficulties in each domain. The combination of these three will change technology and advance a number of fields that will benefit academics and experts in industry, fostering improved service delivery and enhancing corporate structures. The convergence will change the game since it will address security and data privacy concerns.

articleTitle: A Review of the Catalysts System Used for Cross Coupling Reaction (Photo-Catalysts, Dual Catalysts, Pd, Fe and Nano-Particles)
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The economic importance of cross coupling reactions has seen researchers explore all possible ways of making the reaction process more efficient and sustainable.
