A key aspect of the cross coupling reaction is the type and nature of the catalysts system used, which could have a major impact on certain desired reaction variables like cost of production, percentage conversion, sustainability of process etc. The catalysts system used for cross coupling keeps evolving form the pioneering palladium catalysts system used by Suzuki-Miyaura to other transition metals catalysts, photo-catalyst, dual catalysts and Nano-particles catalysts system. This review paper explores the available catalysts system for cross coupling reactions and the advantages obtained by using them as could be seen in the recent works of different researchers. Palladium which has been a consistent catalysts system for cross coupling due to it reported effectiveness and percentage conversion value, is gradually been replaced by more sustainable, green, cheap and also effective catalysts system like the photo-catalyst, dual catalysts and N ano-catalysts system. Recent works that explores the advantages derived from using the different catalysts system and future trends in the field of synthetic cross coupling reaction were highlighted in this paper.

articleTitle: Multi-Disease Detection of Diabetes and Breast Cancer Using The Doctor Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) models using physiological signals and historical medical data to identify ailments are slowly gaining popularity. However, data about diseases becomes available incrementally over time and the behavior of diseases themselves could evolve over time. These factors require the ML models to be re-trained with the new data. The common approach of fine-tuning with new data can lead to catastrophic forgetting, where the model forgets what it learnt in prior iterations. Additionally, most disease detection models are trained for the detection of a single disease only. This increases the computational costs associated with ML model training and deployments, which would be critical when considering usage in cost-sensitive locales such as Africa. In this study, we tried to address these challenges by applying the DOCTOR framework, based on a Multi-head Deep Neural Network (DNN) and a Continual Learning, for the detection of diabetes and breast cancer. In a single-disease incremental scenario, the DOCTOR framework beat the baseline performance of the ideal joint scenario with average accuracy and f1 scores of 0.970 and 0.788 for diabetes, 0.875 and 0.805 for breast cancer. In the multi-disease setting, the DOCTOR framework showed the best performance for diabetes, even though it didn't better the ideal joint training scenario on breast cancer. Also, the results on the diabetes were even better than the single-disease scenario, which shows that such a multi-task learning scenario can help improve model generalization.

articleTitle: Home Automation Using Blynk Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The digitalization is trending globally and automation and wireless connectivity are gaining ground and unprecedented. The major goal of automation is to reduce the human interaction to barest minimum. The implementation of smart homes with the utilization of IoT is aimed at bringing the home appliances into control remotely. Smart home is one of the major break - through in the area of automation. This work will x-ray different applications of IoT with special focus on smart homes using Blynk IoT framework. To achieve this, the NodeMCU development board which embedes the ESP8266 microcontroller is programmed to interact and communicate with the relay module and some sensors, utilizing the android app and Blynk platform as interfaces. The integration of these different systems precipitates a seamless control and monitor over appliances like lamps, socket outlet and so on.

articleTitle: Augmented Security Framework using Internet of Things for Tracking Improvised Explosive Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Terrorism and the proliferation of explosives or improvised explosive devices (IEDs) have plagued many parts of the world. This is an issue of serious public and security concern across the world. One of the innovations like the Internet of Things (IoT), with the inherent ability to sense and propagate information about its environment with neighboring nodes in a network, has shown great promise in remotely providing monitoring and tracking information of suspected harmful substances. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Augmented Reality (AR), Robotics, etc. promises even more deliverables for the future in securing our world. This paper proposes a framework that leverages the IoT for continuous dynamic tracking of IEDs, overlayed with augmented geospatial details for guiding security agencies. The proposed framework would serve as a design and implementation guide.

articleTitle: IoT and Data Analytic Framework for DisCos Power Outage Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This paper introduces a real-time monitoring and performance evaluation system designed for electricity supply based on service band tariffs in Nigeria. The system utilizes an Internet of Things (IoT) data logger to transmit power supply logs to a cloud application server. The system underwent testing, and preliminary results from September 1st to 14th, 2023, specifically for Kaduna Electricity Distribution Company (KE DisCo), are presented. The analysis includes parameters such as average daily electric supply, the longest duration of power supply and power outage, and the number of hourly blinks. For a residential building in the KE DisCo service band D non-MD, the evaluation indicates 100% service band performance, with 7 hours and 36 minutes for the longest power supply duration and 10 hours and 36 minutes for the longest outage and maximum of 22 blinks in a day. The system's potential benefits extend to policymakers, consumers, and electricity distribution companies.

articleTitle: A Procedure for Achieving Network-on-Demand for Intent-Driven Purposes in 5G Era Using Network-Slicing Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Network slicing is a key feature of 5G that allows for the creation and running of multiple virtual networks, known as “slices,” on shared infrastructure. These slices can be customized for specific applications and requirements, and offer greater flexibility than previous network technologies. Additionally, the use of network slicing can generate new revenue opportunities through automation, leading to profitable growth at a large scale. This paper understudied the processes involved in achieving this and thereby proposed a sequence of procedures that will seamlessly realise this, the work first considered Slice Network based on the Business request of the industry vertical, then the aggregation of intent based on the request, thereafter assign slice based on the business request, next a check is carried out if the Network policies are met, the RAN-Slicing is employed, finally, it deploys Network Orchestration, which manages, monitor and grants End-to-End Access, this sequence will help network operators in reducing expenses (OPEX) and capital expenditure (CAPEX). The use of this technology will greatly increase operational efficiency and speed up the rolling out of 5G network services. It will also enable operators to offer a range of new services to customers using the same physical network infrastructure.

articleTitle: Safety Compliance Assessment of Menial Workers at the Nile University of Nigeria Female Hostel Site
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Civil engineering projects place an importance on safety and efficiency, but the construction industry frequently fails to implement adequate safety practices. This study evaluates the compliance of menial workers on the Nile University of Nigeria female hostel site with safety standards and procedures. Through a periodic site inspection that included the use of a safety inspection checklist and questionnaires, prospective construction operations hazard and risks were identified and evaluated. The purpose of the study is to reduce or eliminate these hazards and risks by recommending appropriate safety measures. This research contributes to disaster prevention and injury reduction on construction sites and addresses the limited safety regulations and practices in the Nigerian construction industry and emphasizes the need for enhanced safety compliance. This study's findings will benefit construction industry stakeholders, enlighten legal compliance, enhance project finances, improve safety records, and promote a positive reputation. By emphasizing the significance of safety conformance, this study urges the Nigerian construction industry to prioritize safety practices.

articleTitle: AI-enhanced context-aware optimization of RPL routing protocol for IoT environments
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The Internet of Things networks interconnect devices with sensing, communication, and data-driven capabilities, transforming various domains. However, IoT applications also encounter issues of network security, reliability and energy consumption. This paper addresses the vital challenge of designing efficient routing protocols for IoT networks. We focus on RPL, a widely used routing protocol for IoT, which has drawbacks such as ignoring context, causing congestion, and being vulnerable to attacks. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel AI-enhanced context-aware optimization method for RPL in IoT settings. The method involves a context-aware objective function that considers factors like energy, link quality, traffic, and mobility. An AI-enhanced optimization technique that employs reinforcement learning and deep neural networks adapts metric weights according to network changes and application needs. We compare our method with existing approaches (OF0 and MRHOF) through simulations, showing its better performance in improving network reliability and reducing energy consumption.

Author Keywords: Reinforcement learning and deep neural networks for IoT routing
Network reliability and energy consumption in IoT

articleTitle: Towards Renewable Energy Resources Interconnectivity for Optimal Energy Access in the West African Power Pool
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: One of the main goals of the interconnections in the West African Power Pool is to share energy resources. With the abundance of solar and wind renewable resources in the demographic, integrating these energy resources to be shared across West Africa is a viable solution to boost economic activities, energy access, electricity trading and reduce emissions. In this work, an overview of the agencies to enable the adoption of renewable energy in the region is presented. Also, a brief review of works that considered including renewable energy sources in the energy mix has been done. Low energy access is still an issue in the region and to overcome this both off-grid and grid-connected renewable resources have to be considered. Due to the intermittent nature of variable renewable resources, sharing these grid-connected resources within this region is important. Also, proper regulation and utilization of the regional electricity market can facilitate their deployment. This paper highlighted the prospects of renewable energy in the West African Power Pool.

articleTitle: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Structural Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: AI has the potential to revolutionize the way we design, build, and maintain our built environment. The paper provides an overview of various AI branches, including deep learning, neural networks, swarm optimization, fuzzy logic, machine learning, pattern recognition, probability theory, and metaheuristic optimization. It highlights the applications of AI in structural engineering, such as structural health monitoring, modular construction decision making, and vibration control. The paper also examines the limitations, challenges, and opportunities associated with the adoption of AI in the industry. The paper concludes that AI has enormous potential to enhance the efficiency, safety, and sustainability of structural engineering, and that further research and collaboration between academia and industry are necessary to fully realize the benefits of this technology.

articleTitle: Solvent Vapor Annealing of CH3NH3PbI3 Films for Improved Photovoltaic Performance of Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In this study, we investigated how solvent engineering affected the photovoltaic characteristics of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) fabricated using dehydrated lead acetate as the lead source. The photoactive layer was produced by depositing the perovskite solution using a one-step spin-coating method, followed by either 5 minutes of solvent annealing in DMF or IPA vapour or 5 minutes of thermal annealing on a hotplate at a temperature of 90 °C. An inverted planar design was used for the PSC device's construction. Thermal annealing (TA), annealing in DMF vapour, and annealing in IPA vapour were used to form the perovskite active layers. The efficiency of the solar cells produced by solvent annealing in an IPA is 13%, the open circuit voltage (Voc) is 0.977 V, the short circuit photocurrent density (Jsc) is 20.74 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the fill factor is 61.21%. Our research showed that the PSCs produced using solvent engineering methods are have higher PCE, more stable and reproducible.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Collaborative Crop Disease Monitoring in Wheat Production
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This study addresses the critical challenge of crop diseases in global agriculture by introducing a novel approach that combines wheat production, crop disease monitoring, and federated learning. Crop diseases pose a severe threat to food security, making early diagnosis and intervention imperative. Wheat, a staple crop with significant health implications, particularly concerning diabetes, requires comprehensive research and monitoring. Federated learning, a privacy-centric machine learning technique, emerges as a promising solution to this problem. It allows collaborative model training across decentralized data sources without exposing raw data, ensuring data privacy and security. The study's results, based on three models, demonstrate its effectiveness: Fast R-CNNs achieved an accuracy of 91%, recall of 93%, and F1-score of 87%; Mask R-CNNs reached an accuracy of 93%, recall of 95%, and F1-score of 88%; RetinaNet achieved an accuracy of 84%, recall of 89%, and F1-score of 74%. These results underscore the potential of this approach in revolutionizing disease detection and classification while contributing to global food security and sustainable agriculture. The future work involves refining the federated learning model, optimizing GATs integration, exploring advanced privacy-preserving strategies, and expanding applications to various crops and disease categories, promising a significant enhancement in the quality of life for individuals impacted by diabetes and further advancements in AIoT-driven agricultural disease monitoring on a global scale.

articleTitle: Strategies for Enhancing Petroleum Reinvestment Opportunities in Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Reinvestment in Nigeria’s deep offshore sector has declined, impacting the production capacity and revenue. This study explored strategies to enhance reinvestment opportunities in Nigeria, employing a petroleum investment model based on the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 fiscal provisions. Delayed royalty and tax incentives served as fiscal tools that could attract reinvestment options in the model. The study found that these measures boosted the attractiveness of the investment and, encouraged reinvestment options. Results indicated potential for sustainable growth, emphasizing the need for a balanced fiscal approach. Reinvestment scenarios yielded an impressive 35% internal rate of return, Contractor metrics included a $57 million net present value and $105 million net cash flow, informing responsible development decisions.

articleTitle: IoT Programmable Distribution Board
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This paper outlines the design of a programmable distribution board. The main aim of this study is to introduce a modern transfer switch distribution board that can be monitored and controlled remotely. The design introduced here utilizes two microcontrollers, one for controlling the switching of supply lines in a building and the other is used to make requests to and from a dedicated server to control and monitor each line in the system. It was tested on a 3-phase power supply system with satisfactory results. This has not only reduced risk involved in manually operating a distribution board, but also allows the user more control over their power supply/usage, increasing power efficiency in a building.

articleTitle: A Review of Localization Techniques in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: A wireless sensor network (WSN) comprises of sensor nodes (SNs) deployed for various purposes such as target tracking, target monitoring and localization. The rising need for individuals to access localization-based services has given rise to the emergence of localization techniques in WSN s. Localization means acquiring some information about objects of interest from multiple points in a particular location or area. Applications of localization can be found in autonomous vehicles, Internet of Things etc. This study presents an analysis and review of localization techniques in WSNs. We identified the merits and the demerits of different localization techniques. Future research on localization in WSN should focus on; developing a secure 3-D localization technique for underwater ecosystems and development of an efficient localization technique that can adapt for different environments, both indoor and outdoor.

articleTitle: Predictive Modelling of the Compressive Strength of Laterite - Concrete using Multivariate Regression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In light of limited river sand and escalating costs, alternative materials like laterite are sought as supplements. To minimize trial mixes in concrete composite designs, the idea of predictive modeling becomes attractive. This study focuses on predicting the compressive strength of concrete by partially replacing river sand with laterite using a multivariate regression analysis. Experimental investigations were conducted on various concrete composite samples at varying proportions of replacement percentage (0, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35%, 40%, 45%, and 50%). Compressive strength tests were performed after curing the samples for 28 days. The relationship between compressive strength and independent constituent variables was determined through regression analysis using the least squares regression method. The developed model was validated using experimental data. In evaluating the model, the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ) obtained was 0.98, and the root mean square error (RMSE) was 0.33, demonstrating the model's effectiveness in predicting strength. The highest strength of 33.56N/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was recorded at 25% replacement level.

articleTitle: Effect of process parameter interactions on short shot defect modeling in plastic injection molding
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the effect of interactions of major injection molding process parameters on short shot defects. The factorial design of the experiment and numerical modeling techniques were used. Parameter mains effect and interaction effect sizes were computed, and their significance was tested through ANOVA. It was demonstrated that injection pressure setting and melt temperature were the most influential parameters affecting short shot defects with contributions of 92% and 7% respectively as well as their interactions. The most significant interactions affecting short shot defects involved melt temperature. Knowledge of significant parameter interactions affecting short shot defects could enhance a targeted approach to defect control. The approach and the results presented herein can be adopted in plastic injection molding entities to minimize such defects.

articleTitle: Recent Trends in The Use of Nanomaterials for Wastewater Treatment: A Minireview
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Man's life depends on water in many ways. Worldwide industrialization and water resource exploitation have accelerated during the past few decades. Heavy metals and other pollutants., including effluent wastewater., are released into water streams as a result of industrial activity all over the world. Due to their toxicity., these contaminants are thought to be hazardous to both man and the environment and lower the quality of water. Even in low concentrations., heavy metals can be extremely harmful to living things. Numerous methods have been investigated for treating wastewater for many years. However., the discipline of nanotechnology has recently shown the world how to solve the issue of wastewater treatment using creative and practical methods.

articleTitle: Effect of Annealing Temperature and MoO3 Composition on the Mechanical Properties of PEDOT:PSS-MoO3 Blend Thin Film Layers for Organic Solar Cells and Organic Light Emitting Diodes Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Experimental and computational methods are employed in this study to examine how varying heat treatment temperatures and composition of Moo3nanoparticles, a transition metal oxide (TMO) impact the mechanical properties of PEDOT:PSS/MoO3 thin film blends for organic photovoltaics (OPVs) and organic light emitting diode (OLED) applications. The study primarily investigates the mechanical properties (hardness and Young's modulus), microstructure and surface morphology of solution-processed PEDOT:PSS/MoO3 ink blends of different compositions prepared at temperature regimes between 60 to 120 °C. Nanoindentation is used to investigate mechanical properties and Scanning Probe Microscopy to examine the surface morphological and microstructural changes. Mechanical maps and statistical deconvolutions are used to show the distribution of mechanical properties and phases respectively in the PEDOT:PSS/Mo03 thin film blends at the different annealing temperatures (60 - 120 °C). The experimental and computational results lead to the conclusion that incorporating different percentages of Moo3into PEDOT:PSS can, depending on the blended ratio improve the microstructure, mechanical properties and surface morphology of the PEDOT:PSS/MoO3 blends. Lightly doped PEDOT:PSS/MoO3 blends (1:0.1, 1:0.3), generally exhibit improved surface morphologies, enhanced elastic modulus and hardness, suitable for applications in efficient and mechanically durable electronic devices.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Traffic Flow Characteristics of Bus Stops Along Major Arterials in Abuja
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Highway plays a strategic and important role in economic development. Every year, there is an increase in the number of vehicles using the same transport facilities and because of this, the traffic load becomes higher leading to increase in basic cost of transportation as the highway is the most available means of transportation for everyday commuters to move to various destinations in Abuja. Bus stops are an essential part of the road infrastructure and are essential for managing traffic and congestion. The main purpose of this research was to evaluate the effects of bus stops and its characteristics on traffic flow (traffic monitoring), analysis was done using Geographical Information System tool to locate the legal and illegal points which were used as bus stop location. The research was designed to investigate traffic flow characteristics in the areas of bus stops along the major roads in Abuja. It was observed that a high number of bus stop locations are illegal bus stops; from the GIS analysis, it was observed that 4 of the 9 bus stop locations on Kubwa Expressway are illegal stop location and 16 of the 22 stop points on Airport Road are illegal locations of bus stop. Field data was then collected using two Sierzega traffic counters on two sections (point A- Before bus stop, point B – At bus stop) along Kubwa expressway. The results from the traffic monitoring show that the average speeds recorded before the bus stop are significantly higher compared to that of the bus stop which has led to the conclusion that bus stops generally have significant effect on traffic flow. articleTitle: Green and Sustainable Architectural Review for Low-Income Households
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Green architecture is a term used to define architectural practices that have reduced or limited negative risks to the ecosystem. Green architecture does not only talk about the design and construction practices that reduce the contamination of the surrounding environment but also reduces energy wastage and utilises the amount of energy that can be produced without wasting it. The terms green and sustainability are often used in conjunction with each other. Sustainability takes into consideration the readily affordable local resources, their cost efficiency, and their long-term uses in the building sector. Sustainability of materials in this paper aims at providing greener options in the building sector without being an economic burden on low-income households. The research methodology adopted in this work is explanatory analysis for green, sustainable, low-income households and bibliometric analysis. Data was collected for this through extensive research of related writings. This paper highlights the various natural materials that can be used interchangeably with existing commonly used components and their benefit to the ecosystem. It also highlights ways buildings can efficiently recycle and use renewable sources of energy to provide thermal comfort. This research also gives a better understanding of green buildings for low-income that will help improve the quality of life.

articleTitle: Design and Construction of Secure Door Lock System Using RFID Authentication
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Unauthorized access is a very important security issue everywhere. The traditional door locks which include; knob locks, padlocks, cam locks, deadbolts and mortise locks. Although these locks have provided security to some degree, criminals have however devised various means to break through them, they do steal some of these keys and use them or duplicate them, some of these locks can even be opened with so called “master keys” which are keys designed to open different locks. Now, modern technologies have been made and utilized to make more secure locks to make it harder for these criminals to get access to the system. This project research aim is to design and construct secure door lock system using RFID technology.

articleTitle: Enhancing the High-Temperature Rheology of Warm Asphalt Binders Using Micronized Crumb Rubber
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This study investigates the effects of Micronized Crumb Rubber (MCR) on the high-temperature rheology of a PG 64 (80/100 PEN grade) bitumen. The modified warm asphalt binders were prepared with different MCR dosages. Dynamic Shear Rheometer was used to assess the rheology of the modified binders. Complex modulus and phase angle analysis has shown improved rheology with addition of MCR to the binders. This study recommends modifying the warm asphalt binders with 10 % MCR for enhanced high-temperature rheology.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection System Using Initialization-based Few-shot Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) has become an essential means of ensuring the security of a network. It is a system that monitors the state of the traffic running in the network. Few-shot learning is a novel machine learning (ML) approach that has the ability of recognizing novel objects from very few examples. Conventional ML models require substantial amount of data in order to train the model whereas the IDS dataset is imbalanced and is lacking in various categories. In this research, we proposed and implemented a method of using initialization-based few-shot learning (IB-FSL) to improve the performance of the IDS by initializing the weights and by "learning to fine-tune" the data as it detects intrusion. To accomplish our set objectives, we implemented a ResNet-50 on the proposed IB-FSL which gave us a model that initializes the weights such that classifiers for novel classes could be learned from very few labeled examples and a minimal number of gradient descent steps before the application of fine-tuning. The experiment on UNSW-NB15 showed a good performance with an accuracy of 85.96% on less than 2% of the training dataset. We also obtained a precision of 96.18% and F1-score of 92% while other methods such as Decision Tree (DT), Logistic regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB) and Expectation Maximization (EM) clustering used 100% of the training dataset but achieved an accuracy of 85.56%, 83.15%, 82.07% and 78.47% respectively. This model could be used to detect abnormal data intrusions into the network traffic with low false alarm rate leading to improved network security.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Surface-Active Aluminium Oxide from Kaolin Clay for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Aluminium oxide has a wide range of industrial application, whose utilization can be enhanced through the exploration of solid minerals, such as kaolin. This study synthesized γ-alumina from kutigi-kaolin. The kaolin was dried, crushed, sieved with 300 μm sieve size and thermally converted to meta-kaolin at 800 °C. The meta-kaolin was treated with H2SO4 while the extracted aluminium precipitated as aluminium hydroxide by urea and thermally converted to γ-alumina at 800 °C. The characteristics of γ-alumina shows, it to be white in colour, insoluble in water but soluble in dilute acid. The particles were irregular in shape, with a high surface of 236.81 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/g and pore size of 3.02 nm (mesoporous). The Al-O bond was detected at 615 and 1362.98 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> positions in the infra-red spectra while the x-ray diffractogram peaks at 20, 22, 25, 35, 45 and 52.5° matches the gibbsite and γ-alumina phases. The alumina exhibited good thermal stability and relative purity of 36.81 wt. %. The high surface area and low pore size of the alumina indicate its suitability for use as catalyst support.

articleTitle: Recent Trends in Magnesium Metal Composites: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: There is a recent surge in the use of magnesium-based biomaterials. Corrosion is the main disadvantage of magnesium but its low density and elastic modulus, when combined with high biological compatibility, have resulted in significant study and improvement in this subject. Several research efforts have attempted to improve the corrosion and low yield strength of pure magnesium, including composite manufacturing with suitable biological extra reinforcements, alloying, and surface changes. This study elucidated research development in the synthesis of magnesium-based composites for biomedical applications. There have been sustained efforts in creating bioactive, bioresorbable strengthening and manufacturing technologies to outperform present materials.

articleTitle: Towards a Hybrid Arithmetic Smell Agent Optimization Technique for Stability Control of Microgrid System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The persistent need to control load disturbances and instability on power systems to various loads, especially in developing countries like Nigeria, is overwhelming. In an autonomous microgrid, load variation induces disturbance with a magnitude capable of causing power flow instability. These instabilities can result in power equipment damage and subsequently power outage in some designated consumer loads. To address these challenges, a hybrid optimization algorithm strategy is proposed to maintain the microgrid stability and sustain power quality deployment. A hybrid of arithmetic optimization algorithm and smell agent optimization, called the Arithmetic Smell Agent Optimization (ASAO), is conceptualized in this study. The improved algorithm can be used to design an efficient control strategy for coordinating the operation of microgrid systems.

articleTitle: Utilizing Earned Value Management for Tracking and Predicting The Performance of a Project at Nile University of Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The construction sector plays a significant role in providing the constructed infrastructure in an innovative and cost-effective manner. Over the years as technology and engineering keep evolving, construction is becoming more complex and sophisticated hence, the importance of managing projects, especially large scale and mega projects cannot be overemphasized. Scope creep and cost overruns are two of the many negative outcomes that can result from insufficient planning and management of a project. This has greatly affected a lot of projects in Nigeria causing them to be abandoned. Although project cost variations may occasionally be unavoidable owing to inflation and other unforeseeable circumstances, lack of proper planning and design have also made it difficult to create accurate projections of the cost of materials and the overall project's expense, yet projects can be finished on schedule, within budget, and to the required standards of quality and scope while still being considered to have failed. This research paper explains a project management technique which is the earned value management that will help provide solutions to these challenges. The research also aims to know the in-depth knowledge of earned value management in Abuja. The research employed a survey using questionnaires and a case study. From the analysis, the CPI and SPI turned out to be 0.92 and 0.55 respectively showing that the project is behind schedule and over budgeted. There could be some outstanding setbacks that could have contributed to this. The earned value management technique acts as a trigger warning, demonstrating how severely these setbacks can affect the project if they are not properly managed. The research recommends that professional organizations in Nigeria need to educate their members on the benefits of employing EVM by holding workshops, lectures, and conferences on the subject and government bodies should employ the technique more in construction projects.

articleTitle: Development of A Hybrid Near Field Communication Payment System for a Closed Community
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Near Field Communication (NFC) is a wireless technology that enables secure data exchange over short distances, particularly for contactless payments and other applications. By utilizing electromagnetic radio fields, NFC establishes connections between devices, facilitating convenient and secure information transfer. This project focuses on developing a hybrid NFC payment system for a closed community, aiming to address concerns related to fraud, technical issues during online transactions, loss of access to purchased goods or services, and the security and privacy of personal information. The system comprises components such as a WiFi enabled microcontroller, a communication microcontroller, a display, and an NFC card reader, all interconnected on a printed circuit board (PCB) and powered by a regulated voltage supply. The evaluation of the project demonstrates successful collaboration among hardware, software, and firmware, resulting in a fully functional NFC device. Both online and offline transaction processes operate effectively, with transaction history and results accurately displayed on the software application and web application. Overall, this intelligent hybrid payment system, integrating NFC technology, hardware, software, and firmware, provides a secure, efficient, and user-friendly solution that effectively mitigates concerns related to online transactions, ensuring seamless transaction processes and reliable transaction records

articleTitle: Signal Attenuation Modeling and Simulation for 5G and Beyond P2P Wireless Communication Networks in FR2 Bands: Comparison within M-Region in Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: ITU-R categorized Nigeria into four rain regions (i.e., M, N, P, and Q) depending on the atmospheric conditions. Previous works that have conducted rain and attenuation modeling and simulations have assumed similar signal propagation behavior and parameters within locations categorized under the same region. This paper aims to explore these assumptions by conducting an extensive radio propagation simulations of point-to-point microwave links with a clear line-of-sight in order to estimate the total path loss (attenuation), excess path loss, and flat fade margins for each of the locations within the M-regions, i.e., Kano, Sokoto, and Adamawa. Results obtained showed that in all the locations, the loss monotonically increases with distance, with Sokoto having the highest level of signal losses and fading, while, Adamawa has the lowest. The deviation for both total loss, excess loss, and flat fading margin was found to be between 15 dB across the region.

articleTitle: Micro-Grids System: A Review of Control Techniques and Strategy, Distributed Energy Sources and Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Micro-grid (MG) system is presently an ideal solution to actualize the obligation of credible power delivery to power systems in the near future. This paper presents an overview of the various ‘mechanism’ that embodied MG such as Control Techniques and Strategy, Distributed Energy sources and Energy Storage System. The study also highlighted the basic concept that relates to MG.

articleTitle: Agro-vision IoT-enabled Crop Pest Recognition System based on VGG-16
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: It is more difficult to implement recognition of crop pests in the field than the generic object recognition task because of the high variation among crop pest species which usually leads to the misclassification of crop pests from the same class. Furthermore, in deploying these recognition systems to the field, intensive hardware setups are mostly used. To improve the recognition accuracy, this paper proposes an IoT-enabled crop pest recognition system (CPRS) that utilizes Visual Geometry Group (VGG-16) which uses the multi-level learning features obtained from pest images for the automatic classification of crop pests. The Accuracy result of 88.72% obtained validates the reliability and robustness of the proposed method as capable of detecting the presence of pests in different leaf image samples.

articleTitle: Development Of An Interactive Language Learning Application For Children
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Language development in children is a sequential process that starts from cries and babbles to the production of words and phrases. It has been found that children learn to speak by mimicking sounds within their environment. Speech recognition and synthesis applications can be used to improve the language development process. However, due to the differences between speech features of children and adults, speech recognition systems trained on adult speech do not generalize well when tested on child speech. This project implements a web application that is aimed at improving language development in children. The web app is incorporated with a speech recognition system that works well with child speech. It is built using the transformer model which has shown remarkable results on the speech recognition problem. The model is trained using child speech to increase the accuracy when tested on child speech data. The system is designed to be easy to use, child-friendly and efficient..

articleTitle: Network Intrusion Detection using a Hybridized Harmony Search and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems are used to find security holes in a system. However, a number of factors, including irrelevant information, contribute to intrusion detection system's low detection accuracy. This work presents a hybrid intrusion detection system (IDS) that combines the Random Forest algorithm and Harmony Search to address this issue and increase IDS detection accuracy. The proposed method was analyzed using NSL-KDD, and the experiment results show that the model functions effectively.

articleTitle: Determination of the Optimal Blend Ratio of Hydrogen in Natural Gas System Using Physical Properties as Basis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The Determination of the optimal blend ratio of hydrogen in natural gas systems using physical properties as a basis is an important research topic given the increasing use of hydrogen as an alternative fuel source. This research aims to determine the optimal blend ratio of hydrogen in a natural gas system using physical properties such as its Composition, Heating Value, Density, and Wobbe index as the basis of evaluation. Samples of consumer-grade Natural gas and clean Hydrogen gas were sourced in Nigeria. Both samples were used for blending and laboratory analysis. The blend volume ratios of Natural Gas (NG) and Hydrogen analyzed were 9:1, 8:2, 7:3, 6:4, & 5:5 using a Gasometer and Gas Chromatography Machine (CG). The experiment results provided valuable insights into the potential feasibility of replacing natural gas systems with a Hydrogen-Natural gas blend. The result obtained indicated about 2.06% reduction in percentage methane content, 26.35% reduction in gas density, 19.97% reduction in heating value (HHV), 5% reduction Wobbe index for every 10% increment of Hydrogen Ratio. This implies that blending carbon-neutral hydrogen gas into the natural gas systems for the purpose of decarbonization requires adequate compensation for expected changes in properties like heating value, flow dynamics, and process handling. The EUROMOT specification recommends that the percentage change in the wobbe index should be within the limit of +4% and -4% as an acceptable limit of interchangeability of fuel gas. Using the EUROMOT specification on Wobbe index, further numerical analysis affirmed that Natural Gas blended with as much as 25.74% Hydrogen can effectively be a substitute for fuel gas systems that are presently using Natural Gas.

articleTitle: Advances in Cow Bone Ash as a Replacement for Portland Cement in Green Building Composites
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Demand for cement-based building composites due to the increased human population is on the rise. The need for shelter and other infrastructure has led to increased cement production, which contributes to global warming by releasing greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. Over recent years, there have been increased studies on sustainable alternative building materials that could replace Portland cement in cementitious building composites. This study provides an overview of the utilization of cow bone ash in green building composites to replace Portland cement. The study shows that cow bone ash contains a high oxide of calcium and can be used as an alternative sustainable replacement material for cement in green building composites.

articleTitle: Microcontroller Home-Based Security Reporting System using GPS-enabled Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This study addresses the rising threat of theft and burglary by proposing a microcontroller-based security system utilizing GPS technology for enhanced home safety. Comprising a microcontroller unit, Neo-6M GPS module, and SIM800L communication module, the system enables real-time breach tracking and reporting with a user-friendly single-button activation. It ensures swift reporting of precise coordinates and nearby locations to a designated recipient without compromising security. Affordability, adaptability, and effectiveness distinguish this solution, overcoming existing security limitations. The results demonstrate accurate location tracking, rapid message transmission, and timely alerts. Future recommendations include solar panel integration and alternative coordinate conversion methods. In essence, this GPS-based Arduino microcontroller system strengthens home security, ensuring prompt response and homeowner safety.

articleTitle: Engineering Parameters Affecting Blast-Induced Rock Fragmentation: A Short Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Blasting is the only economical way of excavating hard rocks for mining production and civil engineering operations where mucking from the in-situ rock is not feasible. Blasting performance depends upon two parameters: rock and rock mass properties which cannot be controlled and blast design which is controllable and can be optimized. The methods to assess these parameters exist in various research works and difficult to be assessed by the practitioners. This review gathers and discusses the most common empirical methods for assessing these blasting parameters and the models developed to predict rock fragmentation and should interest quarry operators and managers as it will help for preliminary design and adjust according to the field trial results.

articleTitle: Compositional Analysis and Characterisation of Non-edible Plant Biomass for Carboxymethyl Cellulose Production
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This study assesses the compositional analysis and characterization of eight non-edible plant biomass identified as a potential feedstock to produce carboxymethyl cellulose. The materials' contents were ascertained by gravimetric analysis, and they were further characterized using Fourier transforms Infrared spectroscopy. According to the research, cellulose was present in substantial amounts ranging from 33 % to 41 %, with sugarcane bagasse having the highest concentration. The percentage of hemicellulose ranged from 18 % to 28 %, with corn cob having the highest percentage. Also discovered was that lignin content varied between 9 % and 22 %, with mahogany having the highest amount amongst the samples. The FTIR spectroscopic analysis of all eight samples reveals a broad band at around 3300 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, which is caused by the stretching vibration of the cellulose's O-H groups. The observed peaks at 1600 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and 1500 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> correlated to the hemicellulose and lignin's respective C=O and C=C stretching vibrations. Additionally, a significant sharp peak that matched the stretching vibrations in the skeleton of the pyranose ring, C-O-C, was seen at roughly 1050 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Thus, the findings of this study indicate that all eight samples can yield a respectable amount of cellulose, suggesting that these wastes may serve as feedstocks for the creation of biopolymers like carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC).

articleTitle: The Environmental Issues Caused by Constructions on the Biophysical Environment: Nile Uni Campus
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The Nigerian construction sector plays a pivotal role in facilitating infrastructure development and creating employment opportunities, particularly for the country's youth. It is projected that the construction sector will expand by over 4% in 2021, benefiting from a decline in pandemic cases and associated constraints. However, construction activities have significant impacts on the biophysical environment, encompassing both positive and negative outcomes. Negative effects include the destruction of natural habitats, fragmentation of ecosystems, and alteration of hydrological systems. This study investigated a comparative study of the environmental issues caused by construction activities on the biophysical environment, focusing on an ongoing project at Nile University campus. With the objectives of reviewing the environmental concerns, identifying strategies for mitigating the impacts, and conducting studies and questionnaires to propose suitable solutions. This study holds significant importance as it will assist in planning and mitigating potential environmental effects associated with construction activities. By evaluating and quantifying the impacts in advance, decision-makers and stakeholders can make informed decisions and establish measures to minimize the environmental footprint.

articleTitle: A Review of the Application of Digital Image Correlation to Micromechanical Studies of Polymer Electrolytes
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: High-performing lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) necessitate a stable solid electrolyte. When batteries are subjected to external loads, the electrolytes in LIBs are susceptible to irregular deformation distributions, which may result in an asymmetrical porosity distribution. Therefore, these electrolytes must be mechanically robust to withstand pressures and loads, such as significant volumetric changes in anode materials, as well as to prevent dendrite formation, which reduces their efficiency and extends LIB's lifespan. Numerous research methods and tools have been used to examine the mechanical characteristics of LIB components, including tensile, compression, flexural, hardness, and viscoelasticity experiments conducted using the universal testing machine and nanoindentation machine. However, this study discusses the digital image correlation (DIC) technique to examine the mechanical properties of solid electrolytes on a microscopic scale and how this technique has been and can be successfully used to improve our understanding of the strain distribution and effects on LIBs when the solid electrolyte is loaded.

articleTitle: A Review of the Facility Assessment and Management of Nile University of Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This assessment focusses on facility management using Nile University as a case Study. Focusing on maintenance and management of facilities which is an act of preserving facilities in their original functional standard to retain value and sustainability for a very long period of time, The overall facility is the graded with respect to factors such electricals and lighting, ventilation and air conditioning etc., The Level of Service and conditions of the facilities were also determined in conjunction with the students’ satisfaction level using the international Infrastructure Management Manual (IIMM) by adopting both quantitative and qualitative approaches . It was found that most of the buildings are in excellent condition with others in good condition. The Overall Condition Index (OCI) shows that a total of 37 facilities were assessed. 16 of the facilities are in excellent condition, 14 of the facilities are in good condition and 7 of the facilities are in average condition. The Level of satisfaction indicated by students is also excellent plus the level of service of Nile University is generally found to be at expected level. The recreational facilities are also found to be in excellent condition. The study concludes that there should be a development in the effective preventive maintenance of facilities in the institution and facilities should be regularly maintained to guide against failures such as complete functionality failure, structural deficiencies, failure in services or functionality as well as other maintenance works which should be adequately financed.

articleTitle: A Review of Design and Implementation of Computer Based Census Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This Paper Presents a computer-based census management system which is a software application designed to collect, store, manage, and analyze census data electronically. It replaces traditional paper-based methods of data collection and processing, making the census process more efficient, accurate, and secure. The system typically consists of several components that work together to facilitate the census data management process.

articleTitle: Development Of A Portable Incubator For The Detection Of Coliform In Water Using Iot
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Ensuring clean and safe drinking water is a fundamental human right, yet many lack access, leading to waterborne diseases that claim lives globally. This project aims to create an affordable, portable coliform bacteria detection incubator. It employs a light-dependent resistor (LDR) and an IoT-enabled microcontroller (ESP32) to maintain ideal conditions for incubation. The system uses a Digital Humidity and Temperature (DHT11) sensor and heating element to sustain a 35-37°C temperature range, optimal for coliform bacteria growth. An integrated Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) records resistance and temperature data. Collected information is transferred to the microcontroller and streamed to the Blynk app for real-time monitoring. This innovation's portability and cost-effectiveness make it suitable for remote regions with limited access to laboratory equipment. Significantly, it holds promise for advancing low-cost, portable water quality monitoring systems, potentially enhancing public health.

articleTitle: Rapid and Semi-Quantitative Analyses of Ethanol and Xylene Isomers Using FTIR Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The quantitative determination of ethanol in alcohol samples as well as the semi-quantification of xylene isomer proportions in a commercial cleaning solvent were both carried out using the quick, simple, inexpensive, and non-destructive Fourier transforms infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). The results obtained depicts that the commercial alcohol (Smirnoff vodka) and home-brewed alcohol contain 37.22 % and 37.70% of ethanol respectively. Also discovered to be 8 %, 11 % and 69 %, respectively, were the quantities of the xylene isomers namely para-xylene, ortho-xylene, and meta-xylene in the commercial cleaning solvent. The agreement between these results with those from the manufacturing company revealed excellent precision, reliability, and convenience of the technique employed.

articleTitle: An Optimized Solution to Harmonized First-Come-First-Serve Based Multiple Queues Using Sets of Predefined Burst Time
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: There are many scheduling algorithms in existence today, each with key features, advantages, and drawbacks. Scheduling algorithms are the solutions to queuing problems in computing environment which also has real life application; each scheduling algorithm comes with its unique set of advantages, drawbacks, situations, and environments where they perform at optimal levels. This paper aims to propose an optimized scheduling algorithm which will eliminate possible drawbacks. This is achieved by implementing the solutions which have shown positive results in computing environment and in the business environment.

articleTitle: Ferrock-Based Mortar as a Green Alternative to Ordinary Portland Cement-Based Mortar by Partial Replacement
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Cement is the second most used construction material in the world which poses questions as to whether it can be substituted with another material. The environmental impacts of cement production and use are also questioned; therefore, this project looks at Ferrock, an iron-based binder invented by David stone in 2002. Ferrock has been said to be a greener and sustainable building material. This project investigates Ferrock. During this research, Ferrock was made and its physical properties such as specific gravity, fineness, setting time, and consistency tests were investigated and compared to Cement. This project also looked at the effect Ferrock has on the strength of cement-based mortar by replacing cement with certain percentages of Ferrock. In this project, it was discovered that cement and Ferrock have some similarities which are further discussed in this project report.

articleTitle: Metaheuristic Design of a Mobile Technology and IoT Solution to Combat Insecurity in Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Nigeria has had its fair share of the bad and the ugly insecurity challenges. Despite the efforts of the Security agencies, insecurity seems to be on the increase with hostaging, Kidnapping and other vices that endanger the lives of innocent Citizens. One of the lapses is lack of ability of victims to quickly contact security formations nearer to the scene of incident. This is partly because they neither know nor are able to coordinate to retrieve the phone numbers to contact; yet even at that, dialing with their mobile phones could get them killed. This research paper seeks to design a system that provides the best way for victims to call for help effectively at the time of danger without risking much, nor their kidnappers having a clue to their action. Our solution is a metaheuristic design with the combination of Mobile Technology and Internet of Things (IoT) to help victims of kidnapping, banditry or other insurgencies call for help at real-time and get rescued before it is late. The proposed solution is a security information system that enables the user get timely help when in danger. Technologies deployed include Google Map, WhatsApp and SMS messaging, Phone Gesture and IoT Arduino Sensors. It is expected that ICT deployment for national security would provide the needed security tool to complement the efforts of Security agencies in successfully combating insecurity in Nigeria.

articleTitle: Mechanical Properties of Concrete using fly-ash as a Partial Cement Replacement and Rubber Chips as Coarse Aggregates
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This project report presents an investigation into the effects of incorporating fly ash and rubber additives in concrete mixes. The experimental data obtained from testing various concrete samples are analyzed and discussed in relation to their bulk density, workability, and compressive strength. The results highlight the potential benefits of using these additives, including a decrease in bulk density, improved workability, and increased compressive strength. The findings support the conclusion that fly ash and rubber can be viable and sustainable alternatives in concrete production. The implications of these results are discussed, emphasizing the potential for eco-friendly and cost-effective construction practices. Overall, this project contributes to the understanding of how waste products can influence the behavior and performance of concrete, offering insights for future research and practical applications.

articleTitle: Characterization of Wheat Husk ASH and Calcined Eggshell as Potential Glass Former
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Numerous agricultural byproducts, such as rice husk and straw, bagasse from sugar cane, palm kernel shell, wheat husk and straw, corn cobs, etc, are highly desired for the production of renewable energy and are seen as potential raw materials for high-value products. Because they can be used to extract quality silica and Calcium oxide for borosilicate glass production, this research has demonstrated that these wastes have a significant end value. X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy (XRF) were used to characterize the calcined waste eggshell and wheat husk ash for crystal type, compound identification, and chemical composition. The findings demonstrated that the amount of silica and calcium oxide obtained from agricultural waste could be a suitable alternative source for making glass, with calcined eggshells having a calcium oxide content of 91.7% and wheat husk ash having a silica content of 71.3%. The potential for utilizing the CaO and amorphous silica in the formation of glass is thus intriguing.

articleTitle: Metal Matrix Reinforcements - Fabrication, Applications, and Properties: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Metal matrix composites (MMCs) have emerged as a transformational class of materials, demonstrating exceptional promise for increasing mechanical, thermal, and specialized characteristics across varied applications. This study gives a detailed assessment of current improvements in metal matrix reinforcements, concentrating on their effects, production processes, and applications. Particulate, fiber, and whisker reinforcements are examined for their influence on mechanical, thermal, and specialized characteristics. Various production processes, including solid-state fabrication and liquid-state fabrication, are examined. The evaluation focuses on applications in the aircraft and automotive industries. Addressing obstacles and future prospects in scalable manufacturing and innovative reinforcements, the article gives insights into the growing environment of metal matrix composites over the past years.

articleTitle: Enhancing Perovskite Film Properties Through Solvent Annealing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In this study, we investigated how solvent annealing affected the material properties of perovskite films derived from precursors of dehydrated Pb-acetate. The perovskite active layer was produced by depositing the perovskite solution using a one-step spin-coating method, followed by either 5 minutes of solvent annealing in DMF or IPA vapour or 5 minutes of thermal annealing on a hotplate at a temperature of 90 °C. Thermal annealing (TA), annealing in DMF vapour, and annealing in IPA vapour were used to form the perovskite active layers. The perovskite films made from IPA vapou show the best material properties, and the perovskite films obtained from the thermal annealing process have the poorest material properties. Our research showed that perovskite films produced using solvent engineering methods have better film properties.

articleTitle: Improved Liquid Level Control Design Using Mamdani Fuzzy Inference System.
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In industrial applications such as those in petrochemicals, nuclear, etc. liquid level control is very important: hence we have elaborated a straight forward case of control scenario, that can further be applied in multiple of these areas by simply varying the design to suit each case. We have given preference to the application of fuzzy logic rather than other control methods - hence describing a lot of the background information about it. Then, we move forward to apply the Mamdani type Fuzzy Inference System in demonstrating how the logic works in controlling the liquid level in a single tank system; first using 3-rules, then, 5-rules. We have designed and simulated in MATLAB, the 3-rules and the 5-rules systems. Unlike previous works on these cases, our results show better choices in that, key performance parameters viz rise time, settling time and overshoot, are better than previous results we have seen in literatures. We achieve these better results by varying some parameters, initial conditions and improved Simulink designs; to explore the viability of our chosen method of control. This work also further proves that the FLC is a better controlling method in these areas of its application than other control methods.

articleTitle: Deep-Learning Algorithms for Video Anomaly Detection: A Mini-Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: With the increasing demand for security in the day-to-day lives of people, especially when in public spaces, surveillance system helps to monitor human behavior, prevent illegal activities and detect anomalous events. Anomaly detection in video involves the process of detecting anomalous behaviors that occur in such video. Due to the inefficiency of humans when it comes to surveillance, various algorithms can help to automatically detect these anomalous events in videos. Deep learning is fast rising, which is very useful as it imitates how humans gain knowledge and this helps in the area of surveillance and detection. This study aims to provide a comprehensive review of deep learning algorithms used for the detection of anomalous events captured in videos. This study also captures the datasets available for anomaly detection, the applications and future research directions.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Hamesh and Offices Intrusian Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Insecurity has continued to grow rapidly in Nigeria, living countless of our fellow citizens at the mercy of so-called kidnappers, hoodlums and burglars. This system has been designed to provide security and affordability, it will sever as a secondary security measure which will work together with primary security measures like door locks, etc. The research project is aim to design a system that will quickly respond to illegal entries or break-ins to ensure that security personnel have enough time to respond and detain the culprit. The ultrasonic sensor and PIR sensor will sense the presence of human being with the distance of 25 to 200 centimeter (25 - 200cm). It will send a signal to Arduino Uno to activate the buzzer, LED blink and send SMS using SIM module through mobile phone of the user.

articleTitle: Remote Monitoring System Heartbeat Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In the world Due to the recent development in technology for the field of Medical Science it is much easier to determine the several parameters of the patient via electronic device such as temperature Heartbeat. One of such electronic device is Heart beat monitoring System. The occurrence of persistent illness has set off the highest concern which health sector faces these days. The medical management sector is ensuring to meet the needs of people with persistent illness who need regular monitoring for an extensive time, remotely. The persistent illness has demanded for the increase of telemedicine usage. As such there is need for the Remote Monitoring System Heartbeat Detector. With the ATmega 238 as the heart of the system, it uses the pulse sensor; the analog data collected by sensor is transmitted from the transmitting device. The key contribution of this work is the design of a low cost and compact heartbeat detector circuit that can detect heartbeat and display the result on 16x2 LCD and send the result to GSM Mobile Phone.

articleTitle: Security Threats in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Cloud computing makes it possible to store and access data and programmes online, but it also raises security issues including data breaches, service interruptions, and other dangers like denial-of-service assaults and malware that is specific to the cloud. Strong security measures, routine protocol monitoring and updating, reliable disaster recovery plans, and tight collaboration with cloud service providers are all necessary for organisations to manage these problems.

articleTitle: Optimize Design Strategies for Heat-Integrated Air Separation Columns
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The forefront of energy-saving research in cryogenic air separation units (ASUs) involves the utilization of a heat-integrated air separation column (HIASC). By strategically distributing heat within specific segments of the column, it is possible to enhance the energy efficiency of the HIASC. The current study employed a systematic optimization-based design approach to assess the potential for energy savings in the ASU process while ensuring the production of high-purity products. This approach focuses on mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) techniques to manipulate the column's stages and variables, including the internal heat exchanger area between two diabatic sections of the column. The study findings indicate that implementing the HIASC based on the proposed design approach can result in energy savings of 16.2% and a reduction of over 20% in operating pressure compared to the baseline design.

articleTitle: Intelligent System for Crime and Insecurity Management
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: As the global law enforcement workforce faces unprecedented challenges such as declining numbers and shifting demographics, the need for innovative solutions to manage crime and insecurity is becoming increasingly critical. This paper presents a multifaceted approach aimed at harnessing the power of intelligent systems to address the complex and evolving landscape of crime in societies with diminishing Police workforce in Nigeria. The study provides a comprehensive overview of the demographic shifts leading to a declining workforce and their far-reaching implications on crime rates, public safety, and law enforcement resources. It underscores the urgency of adapting to this new reality and the need for intelligent systems to assist in this endeavor. The paper adopts the object-oriented methodology in the design and development of an intelligent system tailored for crime management and insecurity mitigation. Drawing from the fields of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data analytics, this system employs cutting-edge techniques for predictive policing, resource allocation optimization, and risk assessment. It integrates data from various sources, including crime statistics, demographic data, economic indicators, and social media sentiment analysis, to provide a holistic understanding of the crime landscape. Furthermore, this paper emphasizes the ethical considerations and safeguards built into the intelligent system to prevent bias, discrimination, and privacy infringements. It discusses the importance of transparency, accountability, and community engagement in the deployment and operation of such systems. The study also highlights real-world case studies and pilot implementations of the intelligent system in select regions facing workforce decline. It showcases how the system has contributed to more efficient law enforcement practices, reduced response times, and enhanced crime prevention strategies. The paper outlines a roadmap for future research, emphasizing the continuous refinement and adaptation of the intelligent system to evolving police workforce dynamics. It underscores the importance of ongoing collaboration between researchers, policymakers, law enforcement agencies, and communities to ensure the system's effectiveness and ethical use.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Impact of Height and Bandwidth on Path Loss Exponent of 5G FR1 Wireless Networks at 800, 3500, and 5900 MHz
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: 5G communication systems provide an end-to-end wireless connection to billions of users and devices across the globe. The quality of signals received during radio communication is notably influenced by the behavior of the radio propagation channel. A major parameter used in characterizing this channel is the Path Loss Exponent (PLE). Several works that have estimated and analyzed the PLE mostly considered the effect of distance and carrier frequency. However, the effect of base station antenna height and channel bandwidth on the PLE for 5G networks have not been adequately considered. To address this, the impact of antenna height of base station and channel bandwidth on the PLE within the 5G Frequency Range 1 (FR1) frequencies was investigated in this study, specifically at 800, 3500, and 5900 MHz. The licensed EDX Signal Pro software® with Cirrus high resolution global terrain and clutter data base was utilized to model, simulate and analyze the PLE for Kano City, Nigeria. Results showed that for the tested frequencies, an increase in either base station height or channel bandwidth leads to a significant reduction in the PLE. This study can be utilized by network planning engineers and the wireless research community to further improve network implementation and optimization toward understanding the behavior of signal propagation in 5G networks and beyond.

articleTitle: A Review on Extraction of Rare Earth Elements (REEs) From Coal Using Acid Leaching
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Coal has become a feasible source of rare earth elements (REEs; the 14 stable lanthanides, scandium, and yttrium). It is believed to contain significant amounts of rare earth elements, making it a primary source of REEs which serves as basic raw materials in the production of renewable energy. This review established the feasibility of recovering REEs from coal using acid leaching method. It discusses; the sourcing of REEs from coal, the applications of REEs and acid leaching as an effective hydro metallurgical method for extracting REEs from coal. It also examined the efficiency of methods used by other researchers in extracting REEs from coal. However, the potential of acid leaching as a solution to issues such as: difficult leaching conditions, low recovery and the use of expensive chemicals has not been fully investigated. For a better choice in the extraction of REEs from coal, more study and review are necessary.

articleTitle: Review of Machine Learning Techniques For Class Imbalance Medical Data Set
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Data imbalance threatens a medical dataset where the dominant class is typically viewed as unfavorable. In contrast, the minority class is t supposed to be the positive one, affecting the performance of the machine learning prediction. This aims to examine how resampling strategies in Machine Learning (ML) have recently been used in medical data sets. Many researchers used the preprocessing stage's data-level approach to resample the imbalanced medical data.
