Thirty-two sources were reviewed in which data level techniques of balancing the imbalanced data were applied to medical datasets spanning 2015 to 2022, with oversampling methods outperforming the under-sampling methods.

articleTitle: Investigating q-Exponential Functions in the Context of Bi-Univalent Functions: Insights into the Fekctc-Szcgö Problem and Second Hankel Determinant
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This paper draws inspiration from previous studies and established concepts regarding coefficient estimates within the domains of bi-univalent and analytic functions. In our research, we introduce a novel subclass, which is associated with the q-exponential function. Our investigation focuses on addressing the Fekete-Szego problem within the class, specifically in relation to the q-exponential function. We furnish approximations for the coefficients in question and determine the maximum potential value for the second Hankel determinant. Furthermore, we showcase the accuracy and meticulousness of these discoveries regarding the boundary.

articleTitle: IoT-Aided Intelligent Irrigation System Using Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Farmers in developing nations are faced with limited technology for smart and economical ways of irrigation. This is worsened by the high cost of imports since most of these nations are import-dependent. Increasing agricultural yield to meet the growing population in most of these nations has led their governments to pursue cost-effective ways of managing water and other resources required for optimum agricultural yield. In this study, the Internet of Things (IoT) and edge computing are proposed to provide an intelligent irrigation system to bridge the irrigation gap. This research was carried out using a greenhouse with a controlled environment i.e., the ambient temperature, air humidity, ultraviolet radiations (UV), soil temperature, and soil moisture content were all monitored and measured in real-time within the controlled environment. These data were collected using field sensors processed using IoT -enabled microcontrollers (Arduino kits). The data were processed via Amazon Web Services (A WS) for ontological capabilities of the system consisting of computational capabilities of IoT server and Edge Server. Internet-enabled mobile devices were used to monitor and adopt preferential yield rates for cultivation. Also, an irrigation sequencing algorithm was developed, which uses predictive machine learning K-Mean Clustering Algorithm to predict a more accurate soil moisture content with minimum standard error and a lower mean square error of 0.11 to the predicted soil content compared to when only SVR with mean square error of 0.12.

articleTitle: Search-Based Prediction of Software Functional Fault Slip-Through
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: pressure to improve software development processes is not new, but today 's competitive environment places even greater emphasis on delivering better services at lower costs. Research and development of technologies to simplify and accelerate software development has been conducted since the existence of software. Never the less, projects typically spend at least 50 percent of their development work on rework that could have been avoided, or at least fixed in a more cost-effective manner. By finding more defects early in the software testing process, much of the rework cost can be avoided. One of the main reasons for high rework costs is that defects leak from early stages, when it is cheaper to find and eliminate them. Fault slip-through(FST) metrics are used to determine whether a fault has passed through the phrase in which it should be discovered. Defects can occur during unit testing, functional testing, integration testing, and system testing stages of a software project. The purpose of this study is to investigate the performance of the Cat Swarm optimization algorithm in predicting the drift of functional bugs during the software testing stage. The results obtained in this work show that the accuracy, precision, recall, f1: of the Cat Swarm optimization algorithm for the functional metric number of fault slip-through are 92%, 83%, 91% and 87%, respectively is show that.

articleTitle: A Review on Biomass Briquettes as Alternative and Renewable Fuels
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The adverse effects of the combustion of fossil fuels on humanity and the environment have made it vital to discover eco-friendly, sustainable, and renewable energy alternatives. Globally, there exists loose biomass, which is agricultural and cultural waste that can be utilised to produce briquettes, a type of solid fuel. Briquettes have played a significant role in the energy generation economies of both developing and developed nations. The production of briquettes involves a series of activities, including collection, transportation, storage, processing, and densification of the feedstock to meet predetermined quality parameters. Rice husk, corn stalk, wheat straw, cassava stalk, groundnut shell, olive husk, palm kernel shell and coconut shell are among the feedstocks for briquettes. In order to increase the cohesive strength of the briquettes, binders are incorporated during the densification process. This study aims to investigate the current state of research regarding the utilisation of biomass-derived briquettes as a viable substitute for traditional fuels. To achieve this objective, a comprehensive analysis of recent literature published between 2017 and 2023 is conducted. This study encompasses essential subtopics, including the accessibility of biomass, the selection of binders, the parameters of the briquette process, and the equipment used for briquetting.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Economic Analysis of Solar Photovoltaic Systems for Households and Businesses in Mogadishu
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The number of people in Mogadishu who use electricity has significantly increased during the past few years. most of Mogadishu’s energy comes from fossil fuels which is nonrenewable energy sources. The use of solar energy to power our day-to-day life has great untapped potential. According to researchers, The amount of sunlight that reaches the surface of the Earth in an hour and a half is enough to meet the world's yearly energy requirements. The purpose of this study is to design, simulate and evaluate solar photovoltaic system for residential and business in Mogadishu using PVsyst software and the load estimation for the two cases based on the average primary load profile of each category. Case one, for the residential household we designed an off-grid PV system that generates 3163 kwh/year. and its performance is 71.8% which is good, Also, we compared the costs of Off-Grid and the utility grid for 15 years, the result shows that Off-Grid has a cost savings of 5263 dollars. Case two, for the business we designed (JUST) compos 3 a Grid-Connected PV system that generates 104Mw.h/year, and its performance was 79.6% which is good. Also, we compared the costs of Grid-Connected and the Utility Grid for 15years and the result shows that the Grid-Connected has a saving cost of 656593 dollars.

articleTitle: Utilizing Renewable Energy Sources in Nigeria's Energy Production for Sustainable Development
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Despite being a big supplier of natural gas and petroleum, Nigeria routinely has unpredicted electricity supplies. Doing business in Nigeria is challenging due to the ineffective generation and distribution of power. In this way, Nigeria recognizes the value of clean and renewable energy sources in addressing its power shortage. Nigeria has also had a long history of utilizing renewable energy, particularly hydropower. Numerous studies were done to determine the worth of renewable energy as a compliment to provide Nigeria with the energy required for its national development. Without a doubt, renewable energy sources including Solar, wind, hydro and biomass can be added into Nigeria's higher proportion of fossil fuel-based energy sources to help fulfill demand and the growing interest in climate change around the world. Nigeria is lucky to possess an abundance renewable energy resources, which may boost the nation's energy production capacity and, in turn, assist industrialization and the creation of green jobs for the development of the country. Despite their availability, renewable energy sources are still not being fully used, which prevents them from making a significant contribution to the nation's electrical power output.

articleTitle: Epoxidized Vegetable Oil Based Vitrimers: Future Perspective and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Epoxidized vegetable oils (EVOs) have emerged as a sustainable and versatile class of materials, enriched by their renewable origin and unique chemical structure. This comprehensive review examines the evolving landscape of EVO-based vitrimers, exploring their potential and challenges. The introduction of epoxy groups into vegetable oil triglycerides endows EVOs with properties such as high epoxide content, functional reactivity, and thermosetting behavior. These attributes, coupled with their renewability, make EVOs compelling candidates for a range of applications. We discuss the synthesis methods of EVO-based vitrimers, their mechanical and thermal characteristics, and potential applications in industries striving for sustainable alternatives. Despite their promise, challenges including reactivity, use of appropriate dynamic bonds and processing issues are examined. The environmental benefits and economic considerations of EVO-based vitrimers are also addressed. By providing insights into the future outlook and hurdles, this review contributes to advancing the utilization of EVO-based vitrimers in the pursuit of sustainable materials and technologies.

articleTitle: Simple Smart Traffic Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In many Nigerian cities as well as other nations, traffic congestion is a serious issue. Traffic congestion is a result of signal failure, ineffective law enforcement, and inadequate traffic management. Congestion has a detrimental effect on the economy, the environment, and everyone's quality of life. Therefore, it is imperative that the traffic congestion issue be managed adequately. There are numerous techniques for managing traffic, including wireless sensor networks, inductive loop detection, infrared sensors, video data processing, and infrared sensors. These are all practical techniques for efficient traffic management. However, the issue with these systems is that they are highly expensive to install, maintain, and take care of during the installation process. This paper therefore designs and implements a simple smart traffic management system, which makes use of a rule-based algorithm in conjunction with a microcontroller and PIR sensors. By taking into account variables like vehicle detection, traffic congestion levels, and predefined traffic rules to make real-time decisions and optimize traffic flow, this rule-based algorithm in smart traffic control systems ensures efficient and safe movement of vehicles on the roads. This system however not sophisticated, offers a smarter alternative to the fixed traffic systems used in Nigeria.

articleTitle: Recent Developments in the Production of Geopolymers from Biomass Ash
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The 21st century thus far has birthed the most advances in science, technology, and engineering. The advent of geopolymer materials in the 1900s has facilitated revolutionary research and studies in their applications in environmental science, materials science, engineering, and medicine. Geopolymers are relatively new members of engineering materials. They are classified as inorganic cementitious materials despite being derived from biomass, which is organic. This mini review explores the origins and synthesis of geopolymers from biomass ash and their unmatched potential in various industries including construction materials, bone tissue engineering, and the manufacture of scratch resistant and antibacterial coating.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Testing Android Applications: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This paper offers a review of current research studies that use reinforcement learning (RL) to test Android applications. The primary purpose of this study is to simplify future research by collecting and investigating the current state of Android app testing approaches using the RL technique. We provide a well-defined criterion comprising of seven key points. The key points are: addressed problems, reasons for using the RL technique, RL algorithms, supported events, testing techniques, validation, and evaluation methods. In the literature, we have analyzed various techniques to evaluate their efficiency. This study showed that model-based testing is the most commonly used testing technique. Q-learning is the best algorithm in terms of predictive accuracy. We identified that code coverage is the most widely used evaluation metric and comparison with other tools and techniques is the preferred validation approach.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Total Attenuation of P2P NLOS 5G and Beyond Wireless Communication Systems Operating in FR2 Bands in Nigeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Signal propagation in a particular region differs from another due to differences in atmospheric, climatic and environmental properties, distinct terrain and clutter features. Adequate analysis is essential to understand the radio propagation behavior in a particular region. The ITU-R designated four rain regions, M, N, P, and Q, for Nigeria representing the rain rate distribution and also provided further classifications based on ground conductivity, among other salient parameters. Based on these classifications, this paper utilized the EDX Signal Pro software® to model and simulate a typical Point-to-Point (P2P), Non-Line of Sight (NLOS) link scenarios for 5G networks. The objective was to estimate and compare the total loss, excess loss, and flat fade margins for each rain region in Nigeria. Results obtained from the comparison showed that signals propagating in region N experience the highest level of losses and fading, while, region Q has the least losses and fading.

articleTitle: Radio Environment Map Construction: A Mini-Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Radio Environment Map (REM) is a multi-domain radio information of a geographical location. In the contemporary period, the proliferation of wireless communication has played a significant role in driving the advancement of emerging technologies, including edge computing and the Internet of Things (IoT). Consequently, there exists a pressing necessity to optimize the utilization of the limited spectrum resources available. A technical paradigm embraced by Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to enhance spectrum efficiency is the Database-driven Dynamic Spectrum Sharing (DSS) where users with no prime right (secondary user) are allow to opportunistically use the licensed spectrum. The information contained in REM plays a vital role in DSS. This paper reviews the REM concept, the layers of information contained in the REM, REM construction techniques, related works in literature, the state-of-the-art methodology and REM applications.

articleTitle: Advancements in Titanium for Biomedical Applications: A Review of Recent Developments
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Titanium is an inorganic metallic element that has gained significant importance in various fields due to its exceptional biocompatibility, corrosion resistance, high strength-to-weight ratio, and low modulus of elasticity. These properties have made it a crucial material for improving the quality and durability of life. The chemical and physical characteristics of this element have demonstrated dependability and suitability in the fabrication of mechanical components and constructions that can be implanted within the human body. It has been demonstrated to be a viable option for the fabrication of medical instruments and equipment, particularly those utilised in surgical procedures. This review aims to provide an overview of the latest advancements in the utilization of titanium for biomedical purposes, while also emphasising the distinctive characteristics of titanium that render it an ideal material for medical equipment.

articleTitle: A Critical Review of The Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Cyberattacks have significantly increased in frequency and sophistication over time. The detection and prevention of potential attacks are becoming very difficult using traditional cybersecurity technologies. Cybercriminals are experts in using sophisticated techniques and potent weapons to compromise, assault, and hack information. However, contemporary developments in artificial intelligence (AI) techniques demonstrate that AI can play a significant role in defending against the continually expanding cyberthreats posed by malign actors. AI-based solutions can provide powerful and effective cyber defense capabilities in defending against cyberthreats. The main objective of this research is to highlight the applications and challenges of AI in cybersecurity and identify mitigating strategies for addressing these challenges. A number of existing literatures is reviewed to examine the intersection of AI in Cybersecurity. We discussed some exciting new research directions for developing robust and efficient AI-based cybersecurity systems that can promote a safe and secure ecosystem.

articleTitle: Understanding Degradation Mechanisms in Single Crystal NMC Cathodes for Enhanced Lithium-Ion Battery Performance - a Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries have revolutionized portable electronics and electric transportation, but their longevity and performance continue to be the focus of research. Single crystal nickel manganese cobalt (SC-NMC) cathodes are emerging materials for advancing lithium-ion battery technology. However, harnessing their potential requires comprehending the degradation mechanisms which occur during cycling. This review presents an extensive analysis of the intricate degradation processes affecting them. We explore the structural transformations, surface layer formation, and lithium loss mechanisms that govern the capacity fade and voltage decay observed in these cathode materials. By examining the latest developments in diagnostic techniques and characterization methods, we examine the tools available for studying degradation phenomena. Furthermore, mitigation strategies to enhance the resilience of NMC cathodes are explored, elucidating material modifications and protective coatings. Understanding this is pivotal for designing more robust lithium-ion batteries. This review identifies critical research gaps, offering a roadmap for advancements in energy storage.

articleTitle: Control Techniques Review for the Ball-on-Sphere (BOS) System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: There are many important balancing systems in control theory. The Ball-on-Sphere (BOS) system is one of these systems. It finds applications in aerospace, transportation, robotics, etc. The system is a nonlinear multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system where the ball is controlled on the sphere. It is a testing ground, due to its naturally nonlinear, under-actuation, and unstable nature, in nonlinear systems control. Consequently, different techniques have been used to control the system. A review of these techniques of comprehensive nature is presented in this paper. Different reputable publishers were considered using different search engines utilizing different search terms. The techniques include Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG), Sliding Mode Control (SMC), Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Feedback Linearization (FL), Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and their hybrids. It was established that the system is not covered much in the literature. The LQR, LQG, and SMC were found to be the most used controllers to control the system. Also, 93% of the techniques used no optimization. Additionally, it was established that more techniques need to be explored for the system control. Control techniques hybridization and exploration and optimization usage were found to be the major future directions.

articleTitle: Hybridization of Artificial Immune System Algorithms with Other AI Algorithms: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Artificial Immune Systems (AIS) are a class of computationally intelligent systems inspired by the adaptive abilities of the natural immune system. However, AIS has limitations in computational efficiency, scalability, and handling of high-dimensional data. This paper reviews the fusion of AIS with other AI algorithms, including neural networks, evolutionary algorithms, and swarm intelligence, to enhance performance by leveraging their respective strengths. A comprehensive literature review was conducted analyzing over 12 papers on AIS hybridization published in the last decade. The works were categorized based on the integrated techniques and synthesized to identify benefits and challenges. The integration of AIS with the reviewed algorithms showed several benefits such as improved accuracy, faster processing, enhanced optimization and global search capabilities, and the ability to handle uncertainty and vagueness. However, challenges like increased complexity, parameter tuning, and algorithm selection were also noted. This review provides valuable insights into the fusion of AIS with diverse AI techniques for developing novel systems with enhanced adaptability, problem-solving capabilities, and real-world applicability. The identified trends pave the way for future innovations in AIS-based intelligent systems across security, medicine, finance, and other domains.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Availability and Level of Utilization of Fire-Fighting Equipment in Curbing the Menace of Fire Carnages in Public Buildings in CBD Abuja
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This study is an investigation of the availability and level of utilization of fire-fighting equipment in curbing the menace of fire carnages in public buildings in CBD Abuja. The research design adopted survey analysis using primary data gathered from structured questionnaires from selected public buildings located in CBD Abuja. Data were analyzed using multiple regression. The findings revealed that the availability of firefighting equipment and utilization of firefighting equipment showed a positive and significant impact on fighting fire carnages. Also, the level of availability and utilization of firefighting equipment in fighting fire carnages among public buildings in Abuja is a function of physical and non-physical factors. In conclusion, the homogeneity that exists among the fire safety variables as it relates to the fighting fire carnages in public buildings in CBD Abuja call for re-engineering to explore the potential growth merits embedded in the fire safety practices that are yet to be adopted by public building fire safety managers. The positive coefficients of fire safety variables such as availability of firefighting equipment and utilization of firefighting equipment in relation to fighting fire carnages in public buildings is a further indicator that the building can gain further through the long-term focused strategy on these fire safety practices accelerating performance. The study recommends that there is a need for an increase in the level of availability of firefighting equipment in public buildings and adequate attention given to it to match the possible fire circumstance that may arise at any time.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in the Synthesis of Biobased Epoxy Polymer: Replacing Bisphenol A with Sustainable Alternatives
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable and eco-friendly materials has sparked interest in biobased polymers, especially in the field of epoxy resins. This review examines recent progress in producing biobased epoxy polymers as substitutes for environmentally harmful petroleum-derived resins, especially the widely utilized diglycidyl ether of bisphenol A (DGEBA). Several renewable alternatives with comparable or improved performance traits have been developed. The review focuses on five prominent biobased sources for epoxy synthesis: polyphenol, lignin, vanillin, sorbitol, and vegetable oil. This review delves into the chemical modifications and polymerization techniques applied to these biobased precursors to achieve desirable epoxy properties, such as mechanical strength, thermal stability, and curing behavior. Furthermore, the paper discusses the challenges and limitations faced during the synthesis of biobased epoxy polymers, including the issues of cost, scalability, and industrial applicability. By exploring various biobased sources and their utilization in epoxy synthesis, this review aims to inspire further research and innovation in the quest for environmentally responsible materials in epoxy applications.

articleTitle: Welding Processes and Common Defects: A Comprehensive Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This article gives a brief introduction to welding procedures and typical welding problems. As well as more contemporary techniques like laser welding and electron beam welding, it includes a variety of welding techniques such as arc welding, resistance welding, and gas welding. The article also discusses the origins and effects of typical welding faults such as and control methods such as good material choice and quality assurance systems. To ensure the integrity of welded components and structures, it is helpful to understand welding procedures and how to handle frequent faults. porosity, undercutting, partial fusion, and cracks in welded joints. Emphasis is placed on defect prevention.

articleTitle: An Efficient Broadband Null-Steering Beamformer for Interference Mitigation in Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: It's often desirable using a null steering beamformer to mitigate strong broadband signals interference in wireless communication system. This paper proposes an efficient broadband null-steering beamformer based on an improved Davies Broadband Null-steering (DBN) algorithm combined with Improved Constant Modulus Algorithm (ICMA). The designed beamformer can impose adaptive broadband nulls at interferences without knowing directions in the sidelobe region by employing the ICMA for signal adaptation, while maintaining the main lobe toward the desired user direction. As evidenced by the reduced average output power convergence when compare to the existing DBN algorithm, the designed broadband beamformer improved convergence rate by 16.9%. Thus, the new algorithm is observed to have much faster convergence behavior.

articleTitle: Terrestrial Radio Propagation Research Datasets Repository
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Terrestrial Radio Propagation (TRP) involves radio wave propagation from one station to another over the surface of the earth. Radio communication systems have been deployed for broadcasting, mobile cellular, and public safety. Radio propagation planning plays a crucial role in designing and deploying terrestrial radio networks. Radio propagation models (Path loss Models) are utilized during the link budget, coverage, and interference estimations. The models guide radio network engineers in choosing appropriate placements of radio network equipment, such as the base stations. However, the high cost attributed to TRP data collection, lack of open access, and accurate TRP datasets hinders the development of path loss models that can reliably predict outcomes for different use cases. To address this problem, this paper aims to present a robust TRP repository that provides a platform for hosting and disseminating TRP datasets, which the research community could use for path loss modeling. The repository was implemented using the latest technologies, and its performance was evaluated. The system has been deployed for public access.

articleTitle: Simulation Technology in Renewable Energy Generation: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The escalating energy consumption rates and the alarming environmental impacts associated with fossil fuel usage have driven global attention towards alternative energy sources. While nuclear power has emerged as one such alternative, concerns about past reactor accidents and the health effects of radiation release have limited its widespread adoption. Renewable energy, on the other hand, offers a promising solution with minimal environmental harm compared to nuclear power. However, the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources and their inability to consistently supply power present significant challenges for nations aiming to harness these abundant resources. To address these challenges, the integration of simulation technology into energy generation processes has proven instrumental. By employing simulation tools, it becomes possible to identify, control, and even eliminate factors that may hinder energy generation and efficiency. Furthermore, simulation technology enables accurate predictions of the expected energy output from renewable sources. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the recent advancements and applications of simulation technology in renewable energy generation. It elucidates how simulation technology has been successfully integrated into renewable energy systems and discusses its potential to enhance the efficiency of renewable energy generation.

articleTitle: Advances, Challenges and Opportunities in Deep Learning Approach for Object Detection: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Object detection is a major task in computer vision which have a widespread applications across various domains. Recognizing objects from sample images and videos is such a difficult task which literally utilized machine learning techniques. Prior studies have recorded outstanding performance in different object detection problem using deep learning approach. In this paper, we explores the advances in methodologies for object detection tasks, starting from traditional techniques to the recent surge in deep learning. It also discusses the diverse applications of object detection across domains such as healthcare, transportation, agriculture, retail, surveillance, and environmental monitoring. Furthermore, the paper highlights the opportunities and challenges associated with deep learning approach for object detection. Future direction of the limitation in the field such as class imbalance, unavailability of enough dataset, and interpretability were addressed. In conclusion, the paper provides a continuing scholarship in the area of object detection, serving as a valuable resource for researchers, in the field of machine learning and computer vision application for decision making.

articleTitle: A Review on Autonomous Delivery Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: An invention that could change how we deliver goods is autonomous delivery robots (ADRs). They can deliver different types of items through a wide range of spaces, like sidewalks, motorways, and enclosed spaces, including food, packages, and medical supplies. This literature review looks at the current state of autonomous delivery robot research and gives an insight on the various forms of autonomous delivery robots, the supporting technologies for their autonomous operation, and the challenges that remain before general implementation. The literature review concludes with the indication that autonomous delivery robots have the potential to seriously increase the efficiency and convenience of delivery services. However, there are a few challenges that need to be addressed before autonomous delivery robots can become a frequent reality. These include enhancing sensor dependability, addressing public safety concerns, and improving mapping and navigation algorithms. Despite these difficulties, the future of ADRs is bright. ADRs are probably going to become more important as technology develops in the delivery sector.

articleTitle: Reliable SDN Controller Architecture for Integrated Satellite-Terrestrial Network Convergence: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The current 5G era has met expectations for high data rates and low latency, yet falls short in delivering resilient and ubiquitous connectivity. The terrestrial 5G technology, while successful in some aspects, faces challenges due to congestion and limited capacity in emerging applications, as well as geographical limitations and poor ROI. To combat these issues, integrating satellite technology into terrestrial networks has emerged as a solution. However, the cooperative utilisation of both networks remains a challenge. Diverse research and standardisation efforts propose solutions, notably leveraging Software-Defined Networking (SDN). This paper reviews existing work in this area and presents conceptual solutions. The proposed concept targets reliable convergence, achieving access network selection and traffic steering for end-to-end data transmission.

articleTitle: Development of A Remote Monitoring System for Young School Pupils Using Geofencing Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: With the increasing rate of crimes against children and the deterioration of public safety in various cities, parents constantly worry about the safety of their children when they go to school and until they return. To alleviate these concerns, this project aims to develop a remote monitoring system that enables parents to keep track of their children's whereabouts and receive notification messages when the children exceed the specified area. The system employs GPS and GSM technologies to determine the precise location of the child and to notify the parent accordingly. The system is designed to be easily portable by the child, either by carrying it manually, placing it inside their clothes, attaching it to their belt, or wearing it like a wristwatch. The GSM module is programmed to facilitate communication between the module and the child through two methods of communication, both of which are used to determine the child's location. The main function of the system is to activate an alert message and send it to the person responsible for tracking the child when they exceed the specified area. This process can be triggered using SMS, enabling remote communication with the GSM module via a mobile phone.

articleTitle: Energy Theft Detection in Power System Network: Reviews of Studies on Machine Learning Based Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Energy theft is a major issue in the energy industry, causing significant financial losses and reducing the reliability of the energy supply. With the advent of advanced technologies such as machine learning, energy theft detection is becoming more efficient and effective. Machine learning algorithms can analyze large amounts of energy consumption data to identify unusual patterns that may indicate energy theft while highlighting emerging opportunities and challenges in adopting the machine learning base solution. The study highlighted the advantages of machine learning solutions for detecting energy theft and the likely threats associated with its use. Machine Learning models can handle complex and non-linear relationships between energy consumption readings over time and identify the readings that deviate from the modeled relationships as anomalies. This study seeks to present an overview of electricity theft detection solutions and the application of machine learning techniques to tackle the challenge of energy theft. The review revealed that Time-Series and Deep Reinforcement Machine Learning Models were the least used ML Models due to the volume of data and amount of computational resources they required to train the model.

articleTitle: Polymers for Drilling Fluid Formulations: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Drilling fluids are a fundamental part of petroleum drilling. Drilling fluids are necessary for drilling because they aid in well cleaning, drill bit cooling and lubrication, drill cuttings removal, stabilization of the wellbore for improved filtration, and formation pressure control. Numerous additives are added to drilling fluids with suitable rheological and filtration capabilities in order to stabilize these features. Due to their distinctive physico-chemical characteristics, polymers like carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), hydroxyl ethyl cellulose (HEC), guar gum, starch, and xanthan gum, are regarded as significant additives in drilling fluids. These polymers have a significant potential to enrich the rheological and filtration properties of drilling fluids. Over the years, researchers have looked into the use of various polymers to create drilling fluids with improved qualities that can withstand severe wellbore states at extreme temperatures and pressure. The rheological and filtration properties of drilling fluids can be enhanced by using various naturally occurring polymers, which are reviewed in this article.

articleTitle: Development of an Improved Fault Detection and Fault Tolerant Control Systems using Event Based Modeling & Estimation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: An improved fault detection and fault tolerant control system using event-based modelling and estimation techniques is developed to fulfill high standard of reliability and safe operation. The developed system consist of a loop incorporating PID controller, two actuator, process plant and two sensor which are remotely monitored through a GSM network. As the controller identifies a fault in the system, control is transfer to the functional loop and the operator receives an SMS alert of any faults that have occurred. Using event-based modelling and estimation techniques, the developed system was able to capture events and their interactions in the system to have more accurate representation of system bahaviour under normal and faulty conditions. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, real time data were procured from an industrial process and the result indicated that the developed system achieved a 5.05% improvement in system performance under faulty condition compared to the current approach. This demonstrates that the proposed system has enhanced fault tolerant control capabilities in the case of fault and better fault detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Exploring Television White Space as an Alternative for Wireless Broadband Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Advancement in wireless transmission has enabled the communication among multiple devices all over the world, as well as expanding the frontiers of wireless Internet access. As a result of these advancement, numerous devices are questing for wireless connectivity thereby congesting the existing spectrum. If new measures are not taken to reduce depletion of the reserved radio resource, new allocations of wireless Internet access will be impossible, thereby risking the development of the entire wireless ecosystem. The demands for resourceful spectrum consumption have continually driven researchers and stakeholders in the wireless industry to search for spare radio spectrum to offer affordable and reliable wireless connectivity. The TV broadcasting is not fully utilizing the spectrum in some geographical zone. These TV unused spaces called TV White Spaces (TVWS), are well-thought-out to be the probable future resolutions for unavailability of spectrum. The low frequency band (470 to 694 MHz) of the unutilized TV channel has exceptional broadcast features over extensive distances and enables transmissions through high-rise buildings, trees, and mountains. These features allow the applications of TVWS in Internet of Things (IoT), wireless sensor network, wireless connectivity, wireless switching, smart grid and cities, automated transportation, and logistics as well as connectivity in cloud infrastructure. This paper presents a study on the advantages and benefits of television white space as an alternative to wireless broadband connectivity.

articleTitle: Anomaly-based network intrusion detection using Transfer learning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The rapid development of computer networks and network applications, along with the present global increase in hacking and computer network attacks, has increased the demand for stronger intrusion detection and prevention solutions. The intrusion detection system (IDS) is crucial in detecting irregularities and attacks on the network, which has expanded in size and pervasiveness. In this paper, we develop an intrusion detection system based on deep learning and leverage a recent security dataset, CSE-CIC-IDS2018, to implement a more realistic IDS. We proposed an approach for network intrusion detection using Transfer learning to address both the binary and multiclass classification of network attacks. Network features from the dataset are transformed into grayscale images, the images are used as input to the ResNet50 deep learning model. The dataset is imbalanced, therefore, to increase the generalization of model, the imbalance ratio is reduced by using a synthetic data generation model called Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). Experimental results show that our model achieves good performance for both binary and multiclass classification with accuracy of 92 percent for each case. The proposed approach provides a new method for intrusion detection using transfer learning and SMOTE for correcting data imbalance.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Retail Logistics: Fine-Tuning 5G-Cyberphysical Vehicular Networks with AGSA-Driven Path Loss Models
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Non-autonomous vehicles, like the MasterMover electric Tugs, find extensive application in specialised short-range communication settings such as UK's Tesco warehouses. Employing a resilient MasterMover setup, electromagnetic attenuation within the Cyberphysical vehicular infrastructure can be fine-tuned, thereby enhancing supply chain logistics for retail outlets. This study enhances an earlier conventional Agile Gravitational Search Algorithm (AGSA) with outdated path loss models. Through AGSA-driven path loss optimisation, subsequent regression analysis is employed to generate supervised labels for both observed and anticipated path loss behaviors. The findings are useful for new level 3-5 driverless cars operating at 5G/6G spectrum.

articleTitle: Wastes - Types and Usability for Engineering: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The recent spike in advancement of technology that resulted in great industrial growth had also come with its own challenges. One major such challenge is the increase in waste yield across industries. Therefore waste disposal has fast become a major problem especially for heavy producing industries. To stem this challenge, the study and a possibility of recycle of such waste especially for engineering purpose is expedient. This study is therefore an overview of the various waste types and their possible or established usability.

articleTitle: Reinforcement from Biomass Ash for Metal Matrix Development: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The engineering industry is currently witnessing a high demand for composite materials due to their exceptional chemical and mechanical properties. Metal matrix composites (MMC) have become increasingly popular in the composites industry. The incorporation of biomass ash to enhance metallic matrices is a highly interesting topic of exploration. Biomass ash, a byproduct of biomass combustion, is often regarded as waste. The substantial consumption of biomass contributes to environmental pollution. The aim of this review is to enhance our understanding of the use of biomass ash in MMC applications by focusing on its mechanical, physical, chemical, and thermal properties. Varying types of reinforcement used in the matrix formation and areas of application of the MMC were also considered.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Hybrid Photovoltaic Solar Energy System for Off Grid Rural Electrification
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Renewable energy sources are essential around the globe in power generation with solar photovoltaic energy system as one of the major sources. Lack of access to affordable and reliable power in rural off-grid communities affects their wellbeing in terms of economic and social activities. In this paper, Falde community in Arewa LGA of Kebbi State is used as a case study. The average energy demand and peak load for Falde community were 726.65kWh/day and 90.86kW respectively which were used in sizing system components for system configurations. The system configurations include centralized diesel generating set (DGS), centralized photovoltaic (PV) system, a hybrid combination of DGS/PV/battery, DGS/PV, PV/battery, and DGS/battery system. HOMER Pro software was used for simulation and comparative analysis of six different system configurations based on cost, greenhouse gasses emissions, sensitivity, and systems optimization to select the best optimized result suitable for the selected community. The best suitable solutions to electrify and improve economic activities of the selected community out of the six configurations showed that Solar PV system has the least value of NPC (₦433, 823, 300.00), DGS and DGS/PV have the highest energy production of 328, 500kWh/year and finally Solar PV and PV/Battery have Zero emission of greenhouse gasses.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Spectrum Management: Policy and Regulatory Considerations
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The potential of AI in spectrum management, covering dynamic spectrum access, interference mitigation, and adaptive resource allocation is presented. The study highlights the challenges, comprising algorithmic bias, security concerns, and the need for robust data sets. Global efforts towards ensuring radio spectrum support for emerging AI applications are highlighted. Critical considerations for developing and effectively implementing effective policies and regulatory frameworks in AI-enabled spectrum management regime are discussed elaborately. The importance of safeguarding against monopolistic practices and ensuring equitable access to spectrum resources while fostering AI-based innovations in spectrum management was presented. The paper will serve as a reference for policymakers and stakeholders in spectrum resource management.

articleTitle: Malaria Disease Prediction Using Frequency-Based Machine Learning Algorithms and Ensembles Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Malaria is one of the most serious and threatening diseases in Sub-Saharan Africa. Its cases increase drastically during the rainy season. It can spread throughout an infected person's entire body in less than an hour. The diagnosis process is time-consuming, and its accuracy is negatively affected due to the lack of technical tools and infrastructure in many laboratories in malaria-prone countries. Hospitals, however, keep patient data during the diagnosis period. Due to the vast amount of diagnostic data gathered and stored on a daily basis in various mediums such as files, it has become increasingly crucial to develop powerful techniques for analysing and interpreting the data. This analysis aims to extract meaningful knowledge and insights that can significantly contribute to malaria diagnosis and decision-making processes. This paper selected four frequency-based algorithms, namely Naïve Bayes, (J48) Decision Tree, ZeroR, and the OneR algorithm, to develop a hybrid model for frequency-based classification algorithms using the available dataset of malaria diagnoses collected from the Federal Medical Centre in Yola, Adamawa state. The research results indicate that the highest accuracy, 88.4%, was achieved by the (J48) Decision Tree model. Additionally, this research employed ensemble methods to enhance the performance of each classification model. The results demonstrated that the accuracy of the Decision Tree and ZeroR models remained the same at 88.4% and 60.9% before and after boosting, respectively. In contrast, the accuracy of the Naïve Bayes and OneR models increased from 79.9% to 87.0% and from 79.8% to 87.6% before and after boosting, respectively. In conclusion, among the frequency-based classification models, the Decision Tree model consistently exhibited the highest accuracy both before and after boosting.

articleTitle: Overview of Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) Spectroscopy for Biomass and BioFuel Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy techniques have demonstrated both qualitative and quantitative results while providing a quick, inexpensive, and nondestructive examination of biomass. This study reviewed basic information about FTIR techniques as they relate to biofuel production from biomass. The significance of FTIR spectroscopy to biomass studies was revised, and relevant studies were examined. In addition, FTIR applications in hyphenated systems were reviewed. The use of FTIR techniques in research on biomass valorization is a growing field of study that will increase the range of known potential uses for biomass.

articleTitle: Physicochemical and Structural Analyses of Biomass for Bioenergy Production
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The widespread utilization of fossil fuels while driving economic progress has raised pressing concerns about environmental degradation and climate change. As a response to these challenges, the exploration of renewable energy sources has become paramount. Biomass, as a renewable energy, stands as a promising option. This paper presents a comprehensive characterization of three Nigerian biomass sources: cashew leaves, lemongrass, and corncob employing a range of characterization techniques, including proximate analysis, ultimate analysis, scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. These analyses were conducted in accordance with ASTM standards. The combustion characteristics of the biomass unveil their potential as viable feedstock for bio-oil production. The ultimate analysis further demonstrated the environmentally friendly nature of the samples, as they exhibited low nitrogen and sulphur contents (less than 1%), positioning them as sustainable alternatives in the quest for cleaner energy sources.

articleTitle: Neem Leaf Extract As Corrosion Prevention And Inhibition Agent For Mild Steel In Acid Medium
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Azadirachta Indica (Neem) plant extract was investigated as a non-toxic, green, biodegradable, and readily available, cost effective, organic green corrosion inhibitor (OGCI) for mild steel (MS) in 1M HCL and 1M H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> acid media by Gravimetric (Mass Loss), Potentiodynamic Polarization Method (PDP) and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS). Gravimetric, Potentiodynamic and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy results indicate an increase in Neem extract dosage rate in both hydrochloric and tetraoxosulphate (IV) acid, resulting in an increase in inhibition efficiency. Increasing the extract concentration increases the charge transfer resistance (Rct) and decreases the double-layers capacitance (Cdl) because of the adsorption of N eem extract on the surface of mild steel (MS). The polarization results indicate that Neem extract exhibits mixed type inhibition behaviour on metal surface and adsorption fits well with Temkin isotherm model in H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> solution. The adsorption kinetic and energy of adsorption indicate Neem is adsorbed by physisorption. The findings from different characterization techniques, indicate alignment and agreement with Gravimetric method, and confirm the high potential of Neem plant extract as inhibitor for carbon steel in corrosive media of HCL and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and a competing alternate product to existing toxic, banned, and non-biodegradable chemical inhibitors currently in use in Nigeria and around the worldwide.

articleTitle: A Review on Vibration Causes, Effects and Control in Machine Tools
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Machine tool vibration is an acute issue that can have a negative impact on the efficiency, precision, and dependability of machining operations. Vibrations impact the machining operation's background noise, tool life, and the standard of the manufactured art. Thus, these bothersome vibrations have to be subdued while machining. The review abridges the effects of vibration (poor surface finish, increased tool wear and reduced machining accuracy etc.), with a focus on active, passive and semi active vibration which are the techniques to control vibration characteristics and the recent developments on technology involving vibration. Series of operations are reviewed with different approaches to control vibration in their machine tools. This paper offers a thorough grasp of machine tool vibration phenomena, their impact on machining efficiency, and methods for assessment and mitigation. Challenges have been assessed with preferable solutions provided by researchers for future related studies.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Nanop Article From Coal: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Carbon nanomaterials have sparked considerable interest due to their exceptional properties and diverse applications. Carbon dots (CDs) have surfaced as a unique class of zero-dimensional carbon nanomaterials, alongside Carbon Quantum Dots (CQDs), Graphene Quantum Dots (GQDs), and Carbonized Polymer Dots (CPDs). CDs generated from coal, like as coke, coal pitch, and coal tar, have recently grown in prominence because of their abundance, low cost, and ease of synthesis employing green and efficient technologies such H202 chemical oxidation. This review digs into the most recent breakthroughs in coal-based CD production and uses, with a particular emphasis on their potential for energy, environmental protection, biomedicine, and polymer composites. Coal-based CDs provide several advantages, including minimal toxicity, excellent biocompatibility, high chemical stability, and outstanding photophysical characteristics. As a result, they have been extensively explored in biological imaging, ion detection, photocatalysis, and optoelectronic devices. Researchers were able to precisely control the optical properties of CDs by regulating band gaps and introducing heteroatom (N, P, S, and B) doping, taking advantage of the quantum confinement effect and edge effect. Furthermore, the scalability of coal-based CDs holds the promise of widespread applications and the commercialization of environmentally friendly and cost-effective nanomaterials, which will benefit a variety of fields and improve people's quality of life. Despite significant progress, several knowledge gaps remain, demanding further research. These include understanding the structure-property relationship, developing eco-friendly synthetic approaches with improved yield and quantum yield, and exploring the potential of coal-based CDs in diverse application domains. As the research on CDs continues to gain momentum, these nanomaterials are undoubtedly becoming the focal point of scientific endeavors, driving innovations, and addressing contemporary challenges across multiple disciplines

articleTitle: Prioritizing Off-Grid Energy in Nigeria for Economic Recovery
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Studies have shown that economic growth of countries that have shifted significantly towards Renewable Energy Consumption is positively affected. Nigeria has a lot of potentials for off-grid renewable energy generation. The country is, however, yet to exploit the full potentials of its renewable energy resources to achieve the needed economic growth. This paper therefore aims to examine the off-grid renewable energy potentials in the country, and address the need to exploit them with a view to achieving greater energy access, efficiency and to ultimately grow the economy. Solar, wind, biomass and Small Hydro are the renewable energy sources the country is endowed with and can easily exploit. Finally, the paper also examines the policies promoting renewable energy development in the country, and concluded by making recommendations on steps to be taken to prioritize off-grid energy for economic recovery and to achieve a sustainable growth in the country.

articleTitle: Radio Environment Map Construction: A Mini-Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Radio Environment Map (REM) is a multi-domain radio information of a geographical location. In the contemporary period, the proliferation of wireless communication has played a significant role in driving the advancement of emerging technologies, including edge computing and the Internet of Things (IoT). Consequently, there exists a pressing necessity to optimize the utilization of the limited spectrum resources available. A technical paradigm embraced by Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to enhance spectrum efficiency is the Database-driven Dynamic Spectrum Sharing (DSS) where users with no prime right (secondary user) are allow to opportunistically use the licensed spectrum. The information contained in REM plays a vital role in DSS. This paper reviews the REM concept, the layers of information contained in the REM, REM construction techniques, related works in literature, the state-of-the-art methodology and REM applications.

articleTitle: Modeling the Mechanical Properties of Primary Recycled Type II Dental Plaster Blend Using Desirability Optimization Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Dentistry promotes the use of different materials for various dental treatments. This leads to the generation of wastes that result in environmental pollution which are inimical to human health. Incineration and landfill techniques have proven to be ineffective in dealing with this problem. This paper proposes a pragmatic approach where wastes can be recycled and reused. The methodology involved modeling the mechanical properties of primary recycled Type II dental plaster blend, as a basis for recyclability programme using desirability optimization methodology. Three test standards (ASTM D695, ASTM D6272 and ASTM E384) were utilized in determining compressive, flexural strength and vicker hardness properties respectively of recycled dental plaster and the results compared favourably with that of virgin dental plaster. The implication is that dental practitioners can leverage this technology to reduce the harmful effects of wastes on the environment thereby sustaining dental practice and controlling pollution.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Fully Automated Testing Techniques for Android Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The software testing community has continued to research and develop new ways of testing Android mobile applications to ensure an application function as expected and serves its purpose. Given that every testing technique/tool has its strengths and weaknesses. This study aims to present a comparative analysis of fully automated techniques which automatically generate and execute test cases concurrently during runtime. We selected 10 fully automated techniques published from 2013 to 2023 techniques to identify the similarities and differences that exist among them. We clearly define the comparative criteria (such as the exploration method, systematic method, termination criterion, extraction criterion, and scheduling method) used for comparing the selected techniques. The analysis shows that most fully automated techniques adopt an active learning exploration approach for exploring the application under test (AUT). We also observed that only the techniques utilizing the active learning approach are capable of modelling and abstracting the graphic user interface (GUI) of the AUT, others randomly select events to be fired into the AUT.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Factors Influencing Delays on Construction Projects in Mogadishu Somalia
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Construction initiatives are one of the most essential tools available to nations and organizations for bringing strategic aspirations and objectives to fruition. The Somali government, the Turkish government, and private companies are collaborating on numerous construction initiatives. Regrettably, many of these initiatives have been delayed. Construction project delays can have a significant impact on all stakeholders involved, leading to cost overruns, legal disputes, and reputational damage. The purpose of this study was to identify major causes of the delayed construction in Mogadishu, Somalia, to assess the effects of delay on the completion Time of construction projects, and to find and suggest ways to reduce the delay of construction projects in Mogadishu, Somalia using a questionnaire; this research was conducted. A survey questionnaire was administered to 385 respondents to collect data. Using SPSS, descriptive statistical analysis was performed on the collected data. According to the primary findings, changes in project design, inadequate project management, material delivery delays, and unreliable security issues were the most significant causes of delays. The study also found that delays can significantly affect project social problems, particularly in the case of housing, Personal conflicts among laborers, and the tying up of client capital due to project non-completion. These findings suggest that efFor Ts to reduce delays should concentrate on enhancing project management practices, enhancing communication and collaboration among project stakeholders, and addressing material procurement issues. Overall, the study emphasizes the significance of meticulous 1 y planning and administering construction projects to minimize delays and guarantee success.

articleTitle: User Friendly Web Based Deep Learning System for TB and Pneumonia Diagnosis in Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) and pneumonia are two of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide. Both diseases are preventable and treatable, but early diagnosis and treatment are crucial, especially in developing countries. Chest X-ray (CXR) is the most widely used imaging modality for diagnosing TB and pneumonia, but it is time-consuming and subjective to interpret. Deep learning is a subfield within the domain of machine learning that uses artificial neural networks as its primary computational framework for acquiring knowledge from data. Deep learning models have demonstrated efficacy in a range of medical imaging applications, encompassing the accurate detection of tuberculosis (TB) and pneumonia. This paper proposes a deep learning-based system for accurately and efficiently diagnosing TB and pneumonia from CXR images using the VGG19 architecture. The system was trained and evaluated on a large dataset of CXR images from patients with TB, pneumonia, and normal cases, achieving an accuracy of 99%. The authors also evaluated the performance of eight different deep learning algorithms for the classification of normal and abnormal CXR images. The VGG19 algorithm achieved the highest accuracy (99%), followed by DenseNet121 (98%) and Inception V3 (97%). The system is user-friendly and accessible through a web interface, making it accessible to healthcare professionals in all settings, including developing countries. The suggested method has the potential to greatly enhance TB and pneumonia detection and treatment., especially in developing countries. By automating the image analysis process and improving diagnosis accuracy, the system can help reduce mortality and morbidity associated with these diseases

articleTitle: Formed Coke from Coal and Plastic: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The industrial sector has seen a surge in demand for formed coke due to the steelmaking industry's requirements and increased environmental considerations. Conventional coke's environmental impact and limited availability have prompted industries to seek alternative options. Moreover, plastic waste has become a pressing issue, posing health and ecosystem risks that require immediate attention. Formed coke, made from coal and plastics, offers potential benefits such as reduced carbon emissions and waste utilization. It proves to be a more efficient recycling method compared to incinerating municipal solid waste, as it avoids the release of toxic gases. Incorporating plastics into formed coke production improves energy efficiency and reduces carbon footprints. This review critically examines recent literature on formed coke production using various coal and plastic feedstocks, analyzing accessibility and material properties. The aim is to enhance understanding of coal and plastic utilization in formed coke production for sustainable practices in the steel industry.

articleTitle: Characterisation of Corncob, Sawdust, and Ldpe for Enhanced Bio-Oil Production
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: This study characterizes corncob, sawdust, and LDPE (Low-density Polyethylene) as potential feedstock for co-pyrolysis for improved bio-oil production. These feedstock are characterized for possible co-pyrolysis using various techniques, including compositional analysis, proximate analysis, ultimate analysis, Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, TGA/DTA, and Calorific value. The characterization reveals their potential as a suitable material for co-pyrolysis. The synergy of these feedstock will compensate for individual shortcomings, resulting in improved bio-oil.

articleTitle: Exploring Creative applications in the Digital Age: A review of Computer Numerical Controlled Plotter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Computer Numerical Controlled (CNC) plotters have a wide range of applications, including computer-aided drawing, architectural drawing, and printed circuit board printing. These applications can also be extended to serve person with disabilities class by printing signatures and stamps. CNC plotters are developed for diverse uses. However, cost-effectiveness remains a priority. This review examines different CNC plotters designed for various applications, investigating input data types, generating and streaming geometric code (G-code) methods, and communication modes with microcontrollers. Open-source and custom-built software is commonly used for G-code generation, streaming, and parsing. They are fast and contribute to cost reduction. However, a significant drawback is the reliance on a personal computer to run this software. Additionally, the plotting process can become cumbersome and time-consuming when the input data needs frequent modifications. In order to overcome these challenges, implementing a suitable streaming protocol between a transmitting microcontroller setup and a receiving microcontroller that is interfaced with a secure digital (SD) card module could potentially eliminate the need for streaming software. Similarly, generating polar geometric coordinates for simple shapes like circles, straight lines, inclined lines, and arcs based on user-provided parameters can reduce the dependency on G-code generation software. This approach not only saves time but also maintains cost-effectiveness.

articleTitle: Machining and Heat Generation, Pros and Cons: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Machining is an important component in the manufacturing sector especially for hard materials at higher parameters level as it enables the fabrication of complex components. These processes are accompanied by the generation of heat, and though this has positive effects on the workpiece it also has negative impacts on it. This review paper goes into the phenomena of heat generation during machining and its ramifications in the manufacturing business. It investigates the factors that lead to heat generation in depth, including plastic deformation, friction, cutting pressures, and tool wear. The paper discusses the benefits of heat generation, such as enhanced plastic deformation and surface finish, as well as the drawbacks, such as thermal damage and tool wear. The need for additional cooling method research (as some have been discovered to be dangerous to humans causing several health as well as environmental issues), the study of new tool materials and coatings, breakthroughs in modeling and simulation techniques, a partnership between academia and industry, and promotion of sustainable machining practices are among the key recommendations. As the knowledge of heat generation during machining is critical, this review paper is an essential resource for researchers, engineers, and manufacturers looking to optimize machining operations and ensure high-quality product manufacturing while taking heat generation into account.

articleTitle: GAPS-U-NET: Gating Attention And Pixel Shuffling U-Net For Optic Disc Segmentation In Retinal Images
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Segmentation of the Optic Disc (OD) is a crucial procedure in detecting potential damage to the optic nerve in the retina. This is vital for the screening of Glaucoma and Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) which are the leading cause of irreversible loss of vision worldwide. However, manual segmentation is inefficient, expensive, time consuming and unsustainable. This paper presents GAPS-U-NET, a novel framework with the potential for revolutionizing clinical practice, especially in the context of early detection of Glaucoma and DR. It is a modified U-Net architecture that adopts CNN models as the backbone of the encoder path and applies the upsampling operation of periodic shuffling convolution with gating attention for fast convergence of the network and accurate segmentation. The proposed method overcomes three major challenges of existing encoder-decoder techniques for image segmentation, which are shallow networks, reduced feature resolution, and localization accuracy. First, we employ pretrained CNN model to gain the major benefits of very deep networks that can learn very complex functions to extract more discriminative features for OD segmentation. Then the gating attention block is added to the skip connections to ignore irrelevant regions and focus on important features of a specific region. Finally, pixel shuffling is added to improve feature resolution and segmentation accuracy. GAPS-U-NET is trained on the Indian Diabetic Retinopathy Image Dataset (IDRID) and yielded IOU of 92.83% and an accuracy of 99.71 % which shows that the proposed method can be incorporated into Glaucoma and DR screening programs. GAPS-U-NET is modular therefore it can be integrated into other medical image segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: Advent of Artificial Intelligence in Automotive Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has long been a topic of interest and with its constant development and growing popularity and functions, it is no surprise that it has made its way into the automotive industry. For ages, people have done research regarding AI in the automotive industry, and with the increasing popularity of this subject, the research only goes deeper. This paper gives an analysis of previous research under different areas which involve AI in automotives, somewhat singling out autonomous vehicles. We also go into the basis of artificial intelligence, as well as highlight a few challenges which face the integration of AI into the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Rice Husk-Derived Silica: A Sustainable Alternative to Traditional Fillers in Elastomeric Composites
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant increase in the use of natural fibres as resources for fibre-based products, mostly driven by escalating environmental concerns, hence the adoption of sustainable manufacturing procedures through various green manufacturing techniques and processes. Agricultural residues provide the dual advantage of being cost-effective and environmentally beneficial. Rice husk is known to be rich in silica and has the potential to serve as a filler in elastomeric composites, thereby replacing the traditional petro-based fillers, which are unsustainable, hazardous to health, and consume lots of energy during processing. The applications of green materials today are developing consistently, conquering and entering modern markets. This paper investigates the suitability of rice husk-derived silica as a filler in elastomers based on recent research findings. Additionally, this study sheds insight into diverse modification strategies that can potentially augment the mechanical qualities by altering the chemical and physical characteristics of the husk. This work aims to enhance comprehension of the phenomena related to the production of bio-composites using rice husk as a filler material for elasto mers.

articleTitle: Comparison Between the Impact of Rice Husk Ash and Silica Fillers on Water Absorption in Chitosan Membranes
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The surface morphology and water absorption behavior of chitosan based composite membranes were systematically investigated. Rice husk ash content was varied to observe the resulting effects on membrane properties. Scanning electron microscopy reveals distinct variations in surface morphology. Surface irregularities become more pronounced as filler loading increases. Incorporating rice husk ash leads to greater water absorption compared to pristine chitosan membranes, however, this effect is nonlinear. Water absorption increases to a maximum value at two weight percent ash content. Membrane swelling is also shown to deviate from the observed water absorption trend in specific cases. At different filler quantities, the interactions between filler and polymer are proposed to vary. Lower loadings generate interactions that enhance water uptake while higher loadings alter these interactions, but identifying the precise governing mechanisms necessitates additional research. These findings contribute to the greater understanding of composite material design, promising innovative solutions for numerous applications.

articleTitle: Recent Advancements in Corrosion Inhibitor Performance Evaluation and Surface Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Multidisciplinary Engineering and Applied Science (ICMEAS)
abstract: The eco-friendly nature of organic green corrosion inhibitors (OGCIs) derived from plant extracts has generated considerable interest. These inhibitors are non-toxic, readily biodegradable, effective at preventing corrosion, and economical to extract. In the domain of green chemistry, the increased demand for such inhibitors has prompted research on the evaluation of their performance evaluation and surface analysis techniques. This review conducted an in-depth critical analysis of peer-reviewed published works in international scientific journals between 2018 and 2023, with a focus on the development of techniques for evaluating the efficacy of OGCIs and characterizing surfaces to prevent corrosion. The overarching objective is to provide researchers, vendors, and operators with a concise but comprehensive knowledge base. It emphasizes the practical significance of surface characterization methodologies, delves into their implementation in the real world, and addresses obstacles associated with inhibitor efficacy assessment and surface characterization. In addition, it examines the potential avenues for future progress and innovation, and concludes with salient points for future research endeavours.
